<!-- introthm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:intro-A}
The association $\mathbb{Z}_p^d\mapsto (\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la})^d$ extends to a functor
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\{\text{paracompact $p$-adic manifolds}\}&\rightarrow\{\text{analytic stacks over $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$}\} \\
M&\mapsto M^\mathrm{la}
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
\item If $X$ is a smooth $\mathbb{Z}_p$-scheme, then $X(\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}$ is obtained by transmuting $X$ with respect to the ring stack $\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}$, i.e.\ by sheafifying the presheaf over $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ given by 
\begin{equation*}
R\mapsto X(\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R))\;.
\end{equation*}

\item If $M_1\rightarrow M\leftarrow M_2$ are transverse maps of paracompact $p$-adic manifolds, then $M_1\times_M M_2$ is a paracompact $p$-adic manifold and 
\begin{equation*}
M_1^\mathrm{la}\times_{M^\mathrm{la}} M_2^\mathrm{la}\cong (M_1\times_M M_2)^\mathrm{la}\;.
\end{equation*}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end introthm-1 -->
<!-- introthm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:intro-B}
For any $p$-adic Lie group $G$, pullback along the map 
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^\mathrm{la}
\end{equation*}
induces an equivalence
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^\mathrm{la})\cong \mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)\;,
\end{equation*}
where the right-hand side is the derived category of locally analytic $B$-linear representations of $G$ as defined in \cite[Def.\ 5.9]{Porat2}.
<!-- end introthm-2 -->
<!-- introthm-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:intro-C}
Let $G$ be a $p$-adic Lie group. Then there is a fully faithful embedding
\begin{equation*}
\widehat{\mathcal{D}}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{sm}_{\mathbb{F}_p} G)\hookrightarrow \mathcal{D}((\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G^\mathrm{la})\;,
\end{equation*}
where $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{sm}_{\mathbb{F}_p} G)$ denotes the left-complete derived category of smooth $G$-representations on solid $\mathbb{F}_p$-modules.
<!-- end introthm-3 -->
<!-- introthm-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:intro-D}
Assume that $G$ is a compact $p$-adic Lie group and let $*\coloneqq \mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$. The morphism
\begin{equation*}
f: */G^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow *
\end{equation*}
is weakly cohomologically proper and cohomologically smooth. In particular, we have
\begin{equation*}
f_*(E^\vee\otimes f^!1)\cong (f_*E)^\vee
\end{equation*}
for any $E\in\mathcal{D}(*/G^\mathrm{la})$.
<!-- end introthm-4 -->
<!-- defi-1: body_md -->
Let $R$ be an analytic ring over $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$. A \emph{norm} on $R$ is a map
\begin{equation*}
|\cdot|: \mathbb{P}^1_R\rightarrow [0, \infty]
\end{equation*}
satisfying the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The restriction of $|\cdot |$ along the zero section $\operatorname{AnSpec} R\xrightarrow{0} \mathbb{P}^1_R$ factors through $\{0\}\subseteq [0, \infty]$.
\item $|\cdot |$ intertwines the map $T\mapsto T^{-1}$ on $\mathbb{P}^1_R$ with the map $\lambda\mapsto \lambda^{-1}$ on $[0, \infty]$.
\item Let $\mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{an}}_R$ be the preimage of $[0, \infty)$ under $|\cdot |$. Then $|\cdot |$ intertwines the multiplication map on $\mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{an}}_R$ with the multiplication map on $[0, \infty)$.
\item The composite map
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec} R[\hat{T}]\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_R\xrightarrow{|\,\cdot\, |} [0, \infty]
\end{equation*}
factors through $[0, 1]$, where $R[\hat{T}]\coloneqq R\otimes \mathbb{Z}[\![T]\!]$ is the free $R$-algebra on a topologically nilpotent element, which we equip with the induced analytic ring structure from $R$. Moreover, the map $\operatorname{AnSpec} R[\hat{T}]\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_R$ becomes an isomorphism over $[0, 1)$.
\end{enumerate}
We let $\mathcal{N}$ denote the moduli stack of norms on analytic rings over $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$.
<!-- end defi-1 -->
<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:norms-defi}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Note that we do not impose a compatibility condition between $|\cdot |$ and addition; in particular, we do not ask for a version of the triangle inequality.
\item Any element $f\in R(*)$ induces a map $\operatorname{AnSpec} R\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{alg}}_R$ and hence we obtain a composite map
\begin{equation*}
|f|: \operatorname{AnSpec} R\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{alg}}_R\xrightarrow{|\,\cdot\, |} [0, \infty]\;.
\end{equation*}
Then (i) says that $|0|$ is identically zero while (ii) implies that $|1|$ is identically $1$. 
\item Norms are functorial in the following sense: Given a normed analytic ring $R$ and a map $R\rightarrow R'$ of analytic rings, there is an induced norm on $R'$ given by
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{P}^1_{R'}\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_R\xrightarrow{|\,\cdot\, |} [0, \infty]\;.
\end{equation*}
\item The map $\mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{an}}_R\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_R$ factors through $\mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{alg}}_R$. Indeed, this is because the pullback of $\mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{an}}_R$ along $\{\infty\}\subseteq [0, \infty]$ and hence \emph{a fortiori} along $\infty: \operatorname{AnSpec} R\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_R$ vanishes. \qedhere
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:norms-compactifycover}
Let $\operatorname{AnSpec} B\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec} A$ be a map of affine analytic stacks and consider its canonical compactification $\operatorname{AnSpec} \overline{B}^{/A}\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} A$, i.e.\ the analytic ring $\overline{B}^{/A}$ has the same underlying condensed ring as $B$ and is equipped with the induced analytic ring structure from $A$. If $\operatorname{AnSpec} B\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} A$ is a $!$-cover, then $\operatorname{AnSpec}\overline{B}^{/A}\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} A$ is a $!$-cover as well.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By assumption, the map $f: X\coloneqq \operatorname{AnSpec} B\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} A\eqqcolon Y$ is a $!$-cover and hence the image of $f_!: \mathcal{D}(B)\rightarrow\mathcal{D}(A)$ generates the unit $A\in\mathcal{D}(A)$ under cofibres, shifts and retracts. Indeed, this is because the functor $f^!: \mathcal{D}(Y)\rightarrow \operatornamewithlimits{lim}_{n\in\Delta} \mathcal{D}(X^{n/Y})$ is an equivalence by assumption, where $X^{n/Y}$ denotes the $n$-fold self-fibre product of $X$ over $Y$ and $\Delta$ is the simplex category. One easily sees that the left-adjoint of $f^!$ is given by $(M_n)_n\mapsto \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{n\in\Delta} f_{n!} M_n$, where $f_n: X^{n/Y}\rightarrow Y$ is the projection, and hence full faithfulness of $f^!$ amounts to the counit
\begin{equation*}
\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{n\in\Delta} f_{n!} f_n^!M\rightarrow M
\end{equation*}
being an isomorphism. Applied to $M=A$, this yields $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{n\in\Delta} f_{n!} f_n^!A\cong A$ and since $A\in\mathcal{D}(A)$ is compact, we conclude that $A$ is a retract of $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{n\in\Delta_{\leq m}} f_{n!} f_n^!A$ for some $m\geq 0$, as claimed; here, $\Delta_{\leq m}$ is the full subcategory of $\Delta$ spanned by totally ordered sets with at most $m$ elements.

However, for $p: \operatorname{AnSpec} \overline{B}^{/A}\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} A$, this \emph{a fortiori} implies that the image of the forgetful functor $p_!=p_*: \mathcal{D}(\overline{B}^{/A})\rightarrow \mathcal{D}(A)$ generates the unit under cofibres, shifts and retracts. In other words, we see that $\overline{B}^{/A}$ is descendable in $\mathcal{D}(A)$ and as $\overline{B}^{/A}$ has the induced analytic ring structure from $A$, this shows that $\operatorname{AnSpec} \overline{B}^{/A}\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} A$ is a $!$-cover, as desired.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:norms-normhalfsurjects}
For any normed analytic ring $R$ over $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$, the map
\begin{equation*}
\{|T|=1/2\}\subseteq \mathbb{P}^1_R\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} R
\end{equation*}
is surjective.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By assumption, the map $|\cdot |: \operatorname{AnSpec} R[\hat{T}]\rightarrow [0, \infty]$ factors through $[0, 1]$ and becomes isomorphic to $|\cdot |:\mathbb{P}^1_R\rightarrow [0, \infty]$ over $[0, 1)$. Let $S$ be the Cantor set and pick a surjection $S\rightarrow [0, 1]$. As $\operatorname{AnSpec} \operatorname{Cont}(S, \mathbb{Z})\rightarrow [0, 1]$ is surjective, where $\operatorname{Cont}(S, \mathbb{Z})$ is equipped with the induced analytic ring structure from $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$, there exists a $!$-cover $\operatorname{AnSpec} R'\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} R[\hat{T}]$ such that the composite map $\operatorname{AnSpec} R'\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec} R[\hat{T}]\rightarrow [0, 1]$ admits a lift to $S$ and by \cref{lem:norms-compactifycover} we may assume that $R'$ is equipped with the induced analytic ring structure from $R[\hat{T}]$ and hence from $R$.

Now consider the sheaf $\mathbb{Z}_{\{1/2\}}\in\mathrm{Shv}(S, \mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}))\cong \mathcal{D}(S)$ supported on the preimage of $1/2\in [0, 1]$, where the equivalence is due to \cite[Cor.\ II.1.2]{RealLLC}. Since $S$ is profinite, we can write this as a colimit of constant sheaves supported on clopen neighbourhoods of the preimage of $1/2$ in $S$, which are in turn retracts of the constant sheaf. As the constant sheaf is sent to a connective object under the pullback functor $\mathcal{D}(S)\rightarrow \mathcal{D}(R')$, this implies that $\mathbb{Z}_{\{1/2\}}$ is sent to a connective idempotent algebra $A\in \mathcal{D}(R')$ and hence
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec} R'\times_{[0, 1]} \{1/2\}\cong \operatorname{AnSpec} A
\end{equation*}
with $A$ being equipped with the induced analytic ring structure from $R$. 

Clearly, it suffices to show that $A$ is descendable over $R$. As the pushforward of $A$ along $\operatorname{AnSpec} A\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec} R[\hat{T}]\times_{[0, 1]} \{1/2\}=\{|T|=1/2\}$ generates the unit object under shifts, cofibres and retracts by descendability of $R[\hat{T}]\rightarrow R'$, we are further reduced to showing that the pushforward of the unit along
\begin{equation*}
\{|T|=1/2\}\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} R
\end{equation*} 
is descendable in $\mathcal{D}(R)$. For this, we will produce a section of the map $R\rightarrow R\Gamma(\{|T|=1/2\}, \mathcal{O})$. Namely, observe that there is a bicartesian diagram
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1_R}\ar[r]\ar[d] & \mathcal{O}_{\{|T|\leq 1/2\}}\ar[d] \\
\mathcal{O}_{\{|T|\geq 1/2\}}\ar[r] & \mathcal{O}_{\{|T|=1/2\}}
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
in $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{P}^1_R)$ pulled back from the corresponding diagram in $\mathrm{Shv}([0, 1], \mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}))$ and hence giving a map $R\Gamma(\{|T|=1/2\}, \mathcal{O})\rightarrow R$ amounts to giving maps $R\Gamma(\{|T|\leq 1/2\}, \mathcal{O})\rightarrow R$ and $R\Gamma(\{|T|\geq 1/2\}, \mathcal{O})\rightarrow R$ which are compatible upon restriction to $R\Gamma(\mathbb{P}^1_R, \mathcal{O})\cong R$. However, for $R\Gamma(\{|T|\leq 1/2\}, \mathcal{O})\rightarrow R$ we can just take the pullback of sections along the map $0: \operatorname{AnSpec} R\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_R$ while for $R\Gamma(\{|T|\geq 1/2\}, \mathcal{O})\rightarrow R$ we instead take pullback of sections along $\infty: \operatorname{AnSpec} R\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_R$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:norms-normviapseudouniformiser}
For any analytic ring $R$ over $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$, there is an equivalence of anima
\begin{equation*}
\{\operatorname{AnSpec} R\rightarrow\mathcal{N}\text{ together with }\pi\in R(*)\text{ such that }|\pi|=1/2\}\cong \{\text{maps }\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\rightarrow R\}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
For the map from left to right, we note that $\pi$ determines a map
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec} R\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{alg}}_R\times_{[0, \infty]} \{1/2\}\cong \operatorname{AnSpec} R[\hat{T}]\times_{[0, 1]} \{1/2\}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec} R[\hat{T}]
\end{equation*}
and hence $\pi$ is topologically nilpotent. It is also a unit since 
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec} R\xrightarrow{\pi} \mathbb{P}^1_R\xrightarrow{T\mapsto T^{-1}}\mathbb{P}^1_R\rightarrow [0, \infty]
\end{equation*}
is supported above $2\in [0, \infty]$ by assumption and hence factors through $\mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{an}}_R\subseteq \mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{alg}}_R$.

It remains to show that any topologically nilpotent unit $\pi\in R(*)$ determines a unique norm with $|\pi|=1/2$. By descent, we may assume that $\pi$ admits all roots in $R(*)$. By \cite[Prop.\ II.1.3]{RealLLC}, the data of a norm $|\cdot |: \mathbb{P}^1_R\rightarrow [0, \infty]$ amounts to the data of a family $\{A_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in [0, \infty]}$ of idempotent algebras in $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{P}^1_R)$ corresponding to the pullbacks of the constant sheaves supported on the intervals $[0, \lambda]$ for $\lambda\in [0, \infty]$. As we must have $A_\infty=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1_R}$, we can assume $\lambda<\infty$ and then all $A_\lambda$ will be idempotent algebras in $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{A}^{1, \mathrm{alg}}_R)=\mathcal{D}(R[T])$. 

By multiplicativity of the norm, we must have
\begin{equation*}
A_{(1/2)^{m/n}}\cong A_1\otimes_{R[T], T\mapsto \pi^{-m/n} T} R[T] 
\end{equation*}
for all $m, n\in\mathbb{Z}$ with $n\neq 0$; as we moreover have $A_\lambda=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\lambda'>\lambda} A_{\lambda'}$ for all $\lambda$ due to $[0, \lambda]=\bigcap_{\lambda'>\lambda} [0, \lambda']$ and rational powers of $1/2$ form a cofinal system among all $\lambda'>\lambda$, this shows that all $A_\lambda$ are uniquely determined by $A_1$. To determine $A_1$, we recall that the map
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec} R[\hat{T}]\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_R\rightarrow [0, \infty]
\end{equation*}
has to factor over $[0, 1]$ and hence there is a map $R[\hat{T}]\rightarrow A_1$. At the same time, the map $\operatorname{AnSpec} R[\hat{T}]\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_R$ becomes an isomorphism over $[0, 1)$ and thus there are maps $A_\lambda\rightarrow R[\hat{T}]$ for all $\lambda<1$. Using multiplicativity once again, we conclude that
\begin{equation*}
A_1\cong \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\lambda>1} A_\lambda\cong \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{m/n>0} R[\widehat{\pi^{m/n} T}]
\end{equation*}
by cofinality and hence also $A_1$ is uniquely determined by the requirement that $|\pi|=1/2$. Finally, one easily checks that the map $\mathbb{P}^1_R\rightarrow [0, \infty]$ induced by the above choice of idempotent algebras $A_\lambda$ is always a norm on $R$, which finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:norms-pres}
We have 
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{N}\cong \operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\,\big/\,\overline{\mathbb{T}}\;,
\end{equation*}
where $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$ acts by multiplication on $\pi$.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Combining \cref{prop:norms-normhalfsurjects} and \cref{prop:norms-normviapseudouniformiser}, we already know that there is a surjective map
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\rightarrow \mathcal{N}
\end{equation*}
defined by requiring that $|\pi|=1/2$. Thus, we are done once we show that the self-fibre product of this map is given by $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$. However, given two pseudouniformisers $\pi, \pi'\in R$, the norms $|\cdot |_\pi$ and $|\cdot |_{\pi'}$ induced by requiring $|\pi|_\pi=1/2$ or $|\pi'|_{\pi'}=1/2$, respectively, are the same if and only if $x\coloneqq \pi'/\pi$ satisfies $|x|_\pi=1$, i.e.\ if and only if $x$ defines a section of $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$ over $\operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)$. This yields the claim.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:norms-prim}
The map $f: \mathcal{N}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$ is prim.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Note that $\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$ is prim as the analytic ring structure on $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)$ is induced from the one on $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$; similarly, the map $g: \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\rightarrow\mathcal{N}$ is prim as pulling back along the cover $\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\rightarrow\mathcal{N}$ yields $\overline{\mathbb{T}}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)$, which is a map between affine analytic stacks with the induced analytic ring structure. 

By \cite[Cor.\ 4.7.5]{HeyerMann}, it thus suffices to show that $g_*\mathcal{O}\in \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N})$ is descendable. For this, we use the presentation of $\mathcal{N}$ from \cref{cor:norms-pres} to conclude that $g_*\mathcal{O}$ identifies with the $\mathcal{O}(\overline{\mathbb{T}})$-comodule $\mathcal{O}(\overline{\mathbb{T}})$ over $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)$, i.e.\ $g_*\mathcal{O}$ identifies with the regular representation of $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$. Then the natural map $\mathcal{O}\rightarrow g_*\mathcal{O}$ identifies with the canonical map
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}\;.
\end{equation*}
Noting that sending a power series in $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}$ to its constant term provides an $\mathcal{O}(\overline{\mathbb{T}})$-colinear section of this map, we deduce that $\mathcal{O}$ is a retract of $g_*\mathcal{O}$ and hence $g_*\mathcal{O}$ is descendable, as desired.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:norms-maptatehuber}
Given any Tate Huber pair $(B, B^+)$, the choice of a pseudouniformiser $\pi\in B$ determines a map
\begin{equation*}
f_\pi: \operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\xrightarrow{|\pi|=1/2}\mathcal{N}\;.
\end{equation*}
The upshot of replacing $\mathcal{N}$ by the quotient $\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is that, after mapping further to $\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, all maps as above become identified: Indeed, if $\pi'$ is another pseudouniformiser, then $f_{\pi'}$ is sent to $f_\pi$ by the action of the map $\operatorname{AnSpec}\,(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ induced by the map of topological spaces
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{Spa}(B, B^+)\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_{>0}\;, \hspace{0.5cm} x\mapsto \frac{\log |\pi'(\tilde{x})|}{\log |\pi(\tilde{x})|}\;,
\end{equation*}
where $\tilde{x}$ denotes the maximal generalisation of $x$. We conclude that any Tate adic space admits a canonical map to $\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:norms-primmodr}
The map $\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$ is prim.
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Factoring the given map as $\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\rightarrow */\mathbb{R}_{>0}\rightarrow *$, where we write $*$ for $\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$, we see that the first map is prim by \cref{lem:norms-prim} and hence we are reduced to showing that $*/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is prim. For this, we first note that $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is cohomologically smooth with dualising sheaf concentrated in degree $-1$ by \cite[Thm.\ 4.8.9.(iii)]{HeyerMann} and hence Barr--Beck yields
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(*/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\cong \operatorname{Mod}_{f^!f_!\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}))
\end{equation*}
via $f^!$ for $f: *\rightarrow */\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ and $*=\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$. However, since the map $f$ is an $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$-torsor, we conclude that it is suave with dualising complex $\mathbb{Z}[1]$ and hence $f^!f_!\mathcal{O}\cong f^*f_!\mathcal{O}[1]$ is a shift by $1$ of the compactly supported cohomology of $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ by base change. As the latter is given by $\mathbb{Z}[-1]$, we conclude that $f^!f_!\mathcal{O}\cong\mathbb{Z}$ and as this only admits one algebra structure, we conclude that $\mathcal{D}(*/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\cong \mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square})$ via $f^!$. 

Using the adjunction between $f^!$ and $f_!$, we conclude that $f_!$ identifies with the identity on $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square})$ under the above equivalence, and the same is true for the functors $g_!$ and $g^!$, where $g$ denotes the map $g: */\mathbb{R}_{>0}\rightarrow *$. Now one easily sees that $g$ is prim with the prim dual of $\mathcal{O}\in\mathcal{D}(*/\mathbb{R}_{>0})$ corresponding to $\mathbb{Z}$ under the above equivalence by applying \cite[Lem.\ 4.2.2]{dRStack}.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:norms-suavecover}
The map $\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\rightarrow \mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is suave.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
We already know from \cref{cor:norms-pres} that the map in question is a cover and hence we may check suaveness after pulling back the map along itself. We claim that
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\times_{\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}}\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\cong \accentset{\circ}{\mathbb{D}}^\times_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)}=\{0<|T|<1\}\subseteq\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)}\;,
\end{equation*}
which would prove the lemma as the punctured open disk $\accentset{\circ}{\mathbb{D}}^\times_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)}$ is open inside $\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)}$ and hence suave over $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)$. To establish the claim, we observe that an $R$-point of the fibre product in question amounts to an $R$-point of $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)$ together with a pseudouniformiser $\pi'\in R(*)$ such that the norms $|\cdot|_\pi$ and $|\cdot |_{\pi'}$ induced by requiring $|\pi|_\pi=1/2$ and $|\pi'|_{\pi'}=1/2$, respectively, only differ by the action of $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$. This happens if and only if $|\pi'|_\pi=(1/2)^\lambda$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ or, in other words, if $\pi'$ corresponds to an $R$-point of $\accentset{\circ}{\mathbb{D}}^\times_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)}$. This finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:norms-embed}
Let $S$ be any analytic stack over $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$ and let $\mathcal{N}_S$ denote the base change of $\mathcal{N}$ along $S\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$. Then pullback along the map $\mathcal{N}_S/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\rightarrow S$ induces a fully faithful embedding
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(S)\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_S/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\;.
\end{equation*}
In particular, we have fully faithful embeddings
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square})\hookrightarrow \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\;, \hspace{0.5cm} \mathcal{D}(\mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}})\hookrightarrow \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
We first note that the pullback functor $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_S/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\rightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_S)$ is fully faithful: Indeed, as $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is contractible, this is true for pullback along any $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$-torsor by \cite[Cor.\ II.1.2]{RealLLC}. Thus, we are reduced to showing that $\mathcal{D}(S)\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_S)$ is fully faithful. For this, letting $f: \mathcal{N}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$ be the projection, we will show that $f$ is prim and that $f_*\mathcal{O}\cong \mathcal{O}$. Then any base change $f'$ of $f$ is prim as well and satisfies $f'_*\mathcal{O}\cong \mathcal{O}$ by base change, see \cite[Lem.\ 4.5.13]{HeyerMann}, hence the claim follows by the projection formula.

Primness of $f$ is the content of \cref{lem:norms-prim}, so it remains to show that $f_*\mathcal{O}\cong \mathcal{O}$. Using the presentation of $\mathcal{N}$ from \cref{cor:norms-pres}, this amounts to checking that the augmented cosimplicial diagram
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathbb{Z}\ar[r] & \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\ar[r,shift left=.5ex]
  \ar[r,shift right=.5ex] & \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle X_1^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1} \ar[r,shift left=1ex]\ar[r]
  \ar[r,shift right=1ex] & \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle X_1^{\pm 1}, X_2^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1} \ar[r, shift left=1.5ex] \ar[r,shift left=.5ex]
  \ar[r,shift right=.5ex] \ar[r, shift right=1.5ex] & \cdots
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
obtained from the \v{C}ech nerve of the surjection $\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\rightarrow \mathcal{N}$ is exact. Here, the codegeneracy maps $s^j: C^n\rightarrow C^{n-1}$ are given by $X_{j+1}\mapsto 1$; moreover, the coface maps $d^j: C^{n-1}\rightarrow C^n$ for $0<j<n$ are given by $X_j\mapsto X_jX_{j+1}, X_{j+1}\mapsto X_{j+2}, \dots, X_{n-1}\mapsto X_n$ while $d^n$ is the canonical inclusion and $d^0$ is given by $\pi\mapsto \pi X_1$ and $X_i\mapsto X_{i+1}$ for $0<i<n$.

To show exactness, we produce an extra codegeneracy $s^{-1}$ given by the formula
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:norms-extradegen}
s^{-1}\left(\sum_{\underline{\alpha}}\sum_n c_{n, \underline{\alpha}}\pi^n\underline{X}^{\underline{\alpha}}\right)=\sum_{\underline{\alpha}} \sum_n \delta_{\alpha_1, n} c_{n, \underline{\alpha}} \pi^n\underline{X}^{\underline{\alpha}'}\;,
\end{equation}
where $c_{n, \underline{\alpha}}\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $\underline{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2, \dots)$ is a multiindex with almost all entries zero, for which we set $\underline{X}^{\underline{\alpha}}\coloneqq \prod_i X_i^{\alpha_i}$; moreover, $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker delta and $\underline{\alpha}'\coloneqq (\alpha_2, \alpha_3, \dots)$ denotes the left shift of $\underline{\alpha}$. We first note that $s^{-1}$ is well-defined, i.e.\ that the right-hand side of (\ref{eq:norms-extradegen}) converges: Indeed, we have $|\underline{\alpha}'|\leq |\underline{\alpha}|$, where we put $|\underline{\alpha}|\coloneqq \sum_i |\alpha_i|$, and hence convergence of the right-hand side of (\ref{eq:norms-extradegen}) follows from the fact that the input of $s^{-1}$ on the left-hand side converges. Thus, it remains to check the cosimplicial identities
\begin{equation*}
s^{-1}\circ d^0=\operatorname{id}\;, \hspace{0.3cm} s^{-1}\circ d^j=d^{j-1}\circ s^{-1}\;, \hspace{0.3cm} s^{-1}\circ s^j=s^{j-1}\circ s^{-1}
\end{equation*}
for $j\geq 1$, but this is easy and we omit the details.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:norms-0<p<1}
There is an isomorphism
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|<1}\cong \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Q}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}\times (0, 1)\;,
\end{equation*}
whose postcomposition with projection onto the second factor is given by the norm of $p$. In particular, we have
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\cong \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Q}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}\;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Clearly, there is a canonical map $\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|<1}\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Q}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}\times (0, 1)$ whose second component is given by the norm of $p$. As this is equivariant with respect to the exponentiation action of $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ on the target, it thus suffices to show that $\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\cong \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Q}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}$. For this, we note that $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ acts transitively on $(0, 1)$ via exponentiation and hence $\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\cong \mathcal{N}_{|p|=1/2}$. Finally, by \cref{prop:norms-normviapseudouniformiser}, we see that a map from $\operatorname{AnSpec} R$ to $\mathcal{N}_{|p|=1/2}$ for some analytic ring $R$ over $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$ corresponds to a map $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)/(\pi-p)\rightarrow R$ and this yields the claim due to $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)/(\pi-p)\cong \mathbb{Q}_p$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:norms-embedzp}
Pullback induces a fully faithful embedding
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}})\hookrightarrow \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
We first observe that it suffices to show that $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}})\rightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1})$ is fully faithful. Indeed, this implies the claim as $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\rightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1})$ due to $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ being contractible, see \cite[Cor.\ II.1.2]{RealLLC}. From \cref{lem:norms-0<p<1}, we now deduce that
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|<1})\cong \operatorname{Shv}((0, 1), \mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Q}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}))
\end{equation*}
by \cite[Prop.\ II.1.1]{RealLLC} and similarly for $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|\leq 1/2})$. We conclude that the essential image of $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}})$ in $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|<1})$ embeds fully faithfully into the category $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|\leq 1/2})$ as this essential image precisely consists of the constant sheaves. Due to
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1})\cong \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2})\times_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|\leq 1/2})} \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|<1})\;,
\end{equation*}
it thus suffices to show that $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}})$ embeds fully faithfully into $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2})$.

Now note that
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}\cong \operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle \tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}\,\big/\,\overline{\mathbb{T}}
\end{equation*}
by \cref{cor:norms-pres} and hence the same argument as in \cref{lem:norms-prim} shows that the map $f: \mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}$ is prim. Thus, as in the proof of \cref{prop:norms-embed}, it suffices to show that $f_*\mathcal{O}\cong \mathcal{O}$. To this end, we prove more generally that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T\rangle_{\leq 1}\ar[r,shift left=.5ex]
  \ar[r,shift right=.5ex] & \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T\rangle_{\leq 1}\langle X_1^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1} \ar[r,shift left=1ex]\ar[r]
  \ar[r,shift right=1ex] & \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T\rangle_{\leq 1}\langle X_1^{\pm 1}, X_2^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1} \ar[r, shift left=1.5ex] \ar[r,shift left=.5ex]
  \ar[r,shift right=.5ex] \ar[r, shift right=1.5ex] & \cdots
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
is a cosimplicial resolution of $\mathbb{Z}[\![\pi T]\!]$, where the $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$-action on $T$ is given by division, then the claim follows by modding out $\pi T-p$. For this, we note that the cosimplicial diagram above receives a canonical augmentation map from $\mathbb{Z}[\![\pi T]\!]$ and hence it suffices to construct an extra codegeneracy $s^{-1}$. However, as in the proof of \cref{prop:norms-embed}, one easily checks that 
\begin{equation*}
s^{-1}\left(\sum_{\underline{\alpha}}\sum_{m, n} c_{m, n, \underline{\alpha}}\pi^n T^m\underline{X}^{\underline{\alpha}}\right)=\sum_{\underline{\alpha}} \sum_{m, n} \delta_{\alpha_1, n-m} c_{n, \underline{\alpha}} \pi^n T^m\underline{X}^{\underline{\alpha}'}\;,
\end{equation*}
does the job.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- rem-3: body_md -->
Note that the argument from the proof of \cref{prop:norms-embedzp} is stable under base change. In other words, it also shows that there is a fully faithful embedding
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(S)\hookrightarrow \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\times_{\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}} S)
\end{equation*}
for any analytic stack $S$ over $\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}$.
<!-- end rem-3 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:norms-perfzp}
The fully faithful embedding from \cref{prop:norms-embedzp} induces an equivalence of categories
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{Perf}(\mathbb{Z}_p)\cong \operatorname{Perf}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
As $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is contractible, an application of \cite[Cor.\ 2.7]{Syntomic} shows that it suffices to show that $\operatorname{Perf}(\mathbb{Z}_p)\cong \operatorname{Perf}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1})$ via pullback. Due to $\mathcal{N}_{0<|p|<1}\cong\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Q}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}\times (0, 1)$, another application of loc.\ cit.\ then further reduces us to showing that $\operatorname{Perf}(\mathbb{Z}_p)\cong\operatorname{Perf}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2})$ via pullback along $f: \mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}$. As the proof of \cref{prop:norms-embedzp} already yields a fully faithful embedding $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}})\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2})$, it suffices to show that every perfect complex on $\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}$ is pulled back from a perfect complex over $\mathbb{Z}_p$.

We first prove that any perfect complex is in the essential image of $f^*$. For this, note that the category $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2})$ is equivalent to the category of semilinear comodules $M$ over $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p}{\pi}, X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}$ in $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1})$; by abuse of notation, we also use $M$ to denote the quasicoherent sheaf on $\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}$ corresponding to such a comodule. We begin by establishing the following

\bigskip

\textbf{Claim.} Assume that $M$ lies in the heart of the canonical $t$-structure on $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1})$ and that $M$ is finitely presented as a $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}$-module. Then $M$ admits a surjection from a finite free module on $\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}$.

\bigskip

\textit{Proof of the claim.} For simplicity, write $A\coloneqq \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}$. Consider the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-linear map
\begin{equation*}
\mathrm{ev}_0: M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{coact}} M\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}\xrightarrow{X\mapsto 0} M\;,
\end{equation*}
where the first map is the given comodule structure on $M$, and note that it is idempotent by coassociativity. We let $V$ denote the corresponding retract of $M$, i.e.\ the kernel (not the fibre!) of the endomorphism $\operatorname{id}-\,\mathrm{ev}_0$, and note that $V$ is a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module. Moreover, by construction, the map
\begin{equation*}
V\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p} A\rightarrow M
\end{equation*}
is a morphism of comodules, where we use the trivial comodule structure on $V$. We claim that there exists a finite free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module $W$ together with a map $W\rightarrow V$ such that the composite map
\begin{equation*}
W\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p} A\rightarrow V\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p} A\rightarrow M
\end{equation*}
is surjective, which would yield the desired conclusion.

First note that it suffices to see that
\begin{equation*}
V(*)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p(*)} A(*)\rightarrow M(*)
\end{equation*}
is surjective. Indeed, as $M(*)$ is finitely generated over $A(*)$, this would imply that $V'\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p(*)} A(*)$ already surjects onto $M(*)$ for some finitely generated submodule $V'$ of $V(*)$, which yields the claim. To see this surjectivity, note that $M$ being finitely presented yields $M\cong H^0(M(*)\otimes_{A(*)} A)$. However, this implies that the image of $V(*)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p(*)} A(*)$ in $M(*)$ is dense for the natural topology as counitality and semilinearity of the comodule structure on $M$ shows that any $m\in M(*)$ is a possibly infinite sum of the elements $\pi^k\mathrm{ev}_0(\pi^{-k}m)$ for $k\in\mathbb{Z}$.

This is enough to conclude: Picking a surjection $A^n(*)\rightarrow M(*)$, we see that the preimage in $A^n(*)$ of the image of $V(*)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p(*)} A(*)\rightarrow M(*)$ is dense as well, so it suffices to show that any dense submodule $N$ of $A^n(*)$ is already equal to all of $A^n(*)$. However, letting $e_i$ denote the standard basis vectors, the fact that $N$ is dense in $A^n(*)$ implies that $e_i+v_i\in N$ for some $v_i\in A^n(*)$ all of whose entries are topologically nilpotent. Then the base change matrix from the $e_i$ to the $e_i+v_i$ is invertible, which yields the result. \hfill\qed

\bigskip

To apply the above, take a perfect complex $M$ on $\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}$ and write its pullback to $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}$ as a complex 
\begin{equation*}
\dots\rightarrow 0\rightarrow M^a\rightarrow M^{a+1}\rightarrow\dots\rightarrow M^{b-1}\rightarrow M^b\rightarrow 0\rightarrow\dots
\end{equation*}
of finite projective modules over $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle \tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}$, which we also denote by $M$ by abuse of notation. We claim that the map
\begin{equation*}
M^b[-b]\rightarrow M\rightarrow M\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}\;,
\end{equation*}
where the latter arrow comes from the comodule structure on $M$, admits a factorisation through $M^b\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}[-b]$. Indeed, there is a fibre sequence
\begin{equation*}
M^b\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}[-b]\rightarrow M\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}\rightarrow \sigma^{\leq b-1}M\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}
\end{equation*}
and the term on the right is concentrated in cohomological degrees $\leq b-1$ by flatness of $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle$ as a $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)$-algebra. As $\operatorname{Ext}^{\geq 1}(M^b, -)$ is identically zero by projectivity of $M^b$, this implies that the composite map
\begin{equation*}
M^b[-b]\rightarrow M\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}\rightarrow \sigma^{\leq b-1}M\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}
\end{equation*}
is nullhomotopic and hence admits a factorisation through $M^b\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}[-b]$, as desired. 

This equips $M^b$ with a $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}\langle X^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}$-comodule structure compatible with the one on $M$ and by the claim we find a surjective map $f^*V\rightarrow M^b$ for some finite free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module $V$, where we interpret $M^b$ as a sheaf on $\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}$ via the comodule structure we have constructed. In particular, the induced map $f^*V[-b]\rightarrow M^b[-b]\rightarrow M$ surjects onto $H^b(M)$. Replacing $M$ by the cofibre of $f^*V[-b]\rightarrow M$, which is now concentrated in cohomological degrees $\leq b-1$, and repeating this argument inductively, we obtain a possibly infinite resolution of $M$ by finite free modules on $\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}$. As the proof of \cref{prop:norms-embedzp} already shows that $f_*\mathcal{O}\cong \mathcal{O}$, any map between finite free modules on $\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}$ is pulled back from a map between finite free modules over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ and hence we conclude that $M$ is the pullback of a pseudocoherent complex over $\mathbb{Z}_p$.

To finish the proof, we have to show that if $V$ is a pseudocoherent complex over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ whose pullback $f^*V$ to $\mathcal{N}_{|p|\leq 1/2}$ is perfect, then $V$ is perfect itself. For this, note that $f^*V$ being perfect in particular implies that the base change of $V$ along $\mathbb{Z}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}$ is perfect. Moreover, while this pullback is in general computed using the solid tensor product, this agrees with the algebraic tensor product in our case as $V$ is pseudocoherent and hence our question is purely algebraic and we may ignore the condensed structures. Thus, it suffices to check that $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}$ is a faithfully flat $\mathbb{Z}_p$-algebra. However, this is clear: Being flat over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is the same as being torsionfree and both the special and the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb{Z}_p(*)$ are clearly in the image of the map from $\operatorname{Spec}  \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}(*)$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- rem-4: body_md -->
Using a similar argument, one can also show that the fully faithful embeddings $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{Z}_{\mathsmaller{\square}})\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})$ and $\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}})\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})$ from \cref{prop:norms-embed} induce equivalences 
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{Perf}(\mathbb{Z})\cong\operatorname{Perf}(\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}) \hspace{0.5cm}\text{and}\hspace{0.5cm} \operatorname{Perf}(\mathbb{F}_p)\cong\operatorname{Perf}(\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\;. \qedhere
\end{equation*}
<!-- end rem-4 -->
<!-- defi-2: body_md -->
The algebra of locally analytic $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)$-valued functions on $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is given by
\begin{equation*}
C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\coloneqq \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\varepsilon>0} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\left\langle \pi^{\varepsilon n}\binom{x}{n}: n\geq 0\right\rangle\;,
\end{equation*}
where the algebra in the colimit is obtained by $\pi$-completing the ring
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{Z}[\pi]\left[\pi^{\lceil\varepsilon n\rceil}\binom{x}{n}: n\geq 0\right]
\end{equation*}
and then inverting $\pi$.
<!-- end defi-2 -->
<!-- rem-5: body_md -->
A formal power series $f=\sum_n a_n\binom{x}{n}$ with $a_n\in\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)$ is contained in the ring $C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$ if and only if $\pi^{-\varepsilon n}a_n\rightarrow 0$ in the $\pi$-adic topology for some $\varepsilon>0$. In other words, the $\pi$-adic valuations of the $a_n$ grow at least linearly.
<!-- end rem-5 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:man-eval}
For each $k\geq 1$, there is a well-defined evaluation map
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\mathrm{ev}: C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\times \mathbb{Z}_p&\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle \\
(f, x)&\mapsto f(x)\;.
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
We first observe that there is a straightforward map
\begin{equation*}
\mathrm{ev}: C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\times \mathbb{Z}\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\;.
\end{equation*}
Indeed, for any $x\in\mathbb{Z}$, the binomial coefficients $\binom{x}{n}$ will be integers and hence $f(x)=\sum_n a_n\binom{x}{n}$ makes sense in $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)$ due to $a_n\rightarrow 0$ in the $\pi$-adic topology. As $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle \tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$ is $\pi$-adically separated, there can be at most one extension of $\mathrm{ev}$ from $\mathbb{Z}$ to $\mathbb{Z}_p$ and our task is just to check that $\operatornamewithlimits{lim}_{n\rightarrow\infty} \mathrm{ev}(f, x_n)$ exists in $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$ for any $f\in C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$ and $x_n\in\mathbb{Z}$ converging $p$-adically.

For this, take any $x=\sum_i p^i x_i\in\mathbb{Z}_p$, where the $x_i$ are integers. Our task is to make sense of the expression
\begin{equation*}
\sum_n a_n\binom{\sum_i p^i x_i}{n}
\end{equation*}
in the ring $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$ for any sequence $a_n\in\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)$ satisfying $\pi^{-\varepsilon n}a_n\rightarrow 0$ in the $\pi$-adic topology for some $\varepsilon>0$. As $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$ only gets smaller if we enlarge $k$, we may assume that $\varepsilon k\geq \tfrac{1}{p-1}$. Then \cref{lem:app-binompseries} shows that we can write
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:man-evalexpand}
\sum_n a_n\binom{\sum_i p^i x_i}{n}=\sum_n \sum_{|\underline{j}|=n} a_n\lambda_{n, \underline{j}}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{j}}
\end{equation}
for integers $\lambda_{n, \underline{j}}$ satisfying
\begin{equation*}
\frac{1}{k}v_p(\lambda_{n, \underline{j}})+\varepsilon n\geq \sum_i \frac{ij_i}{k}\geq \max\left\{\frac{\max\{i: j_i\neq 0\}}{k}, \frac{|\underline{j}|}{k}\right\}\;,
\end{equation*}
where we recall that $\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{j}}\coloneqq \prod_i \binom{x_i}{j_i}$, which is in particular an integer. Ordering the multiindices $\underline{j}$ in each inner sum by the largest index $i$ such that $j_i\neq 0$, we see that the $\pi$-adic valuation of the coefficients
\begin{equation*}
a_n\cdot \frac{\lambda_{n, \underline{j}}}{p^{k\lfloor v_p(\lambda_{n, \underline{j}})/k\rfloor}}\cdot \pi^{\lfloor v_p(\lambda_{n, \underline{j}})/k\rfloor}\cdot \left(\frac{p^k}{\pi}\right)^{\lfloor v_p(\lambda_{n, \underline{j}})/k\rfloor }
\end{equation*}
in the sum on the right-hand side of (\ref{eq:man-evalexpand}) grows faster than $i/k$ since the $\pi$-adic valuation of $a_n$ grows faster than $\varepsilon n$ by assumption. In particular, it goes to infinity and hence each inner sum on the right-hand side of (\ref{eq:man-evalexpand}) makes sense in $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$. To see that also the outer sum makes sense, we invoke the second bound from above: in the $n$-th inner sum, the $\pi$-adic valuation of each coefficient is at least $|\underline{j}|/k$ and this goes to infinity as $|\underline{j}|=n\rightarrow\infty$, which finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:man-zpdla}
Let $d\geq 0$. If $C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p^d, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$ denotes the $d$-fold tensor product of $C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$ over $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$, then 
\begin{equation*}
C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p^d, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\varepsilon>0} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\left\langle \pi^{\varepsilon |\underline{n}|}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}: \underline{n}\geq 0\right\rangle\;,
\end{equation*}
where $\underline{n}=(n_1, \dots, n_d)$ is a multiindex, for which we set $|\underline{n}|\coloneqq n_1+\dots+n_d$, and we recall that $\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}$ denotes the product of the $\binom{x_i}{n_i}$ for $i=1, \dots, d$.
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
It suffices to show that
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{Z}[\![\pi]\!]\left\langle \pi^{\varepsilon n}\binom{x}{n}: n\geq 0\right\rangle^{\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}[\![\pi]\!]} d}\cong \mathbb{Z}[\![\pi]\!]\left\langle \pi^{\varepsilon |\underline{n}|}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}: \underline{n}\geq 0\right\rangle
\end{equation*}
for each $\varepsilon>0$, then the result follows by inverting $\pi$ and taking colimits over $\varepsilon>0$. As the solid tensor product preserves derived $\pi$-completeness, both sides of the claimed isomorphism are derived $\pi$-complete and hence we may check it after reducing mod $\pi$. However, then both sides are discrete free $\mathbb{Z}$-modules of countable dimension and the claim is clear by looking at the basis elements.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:man-endos}
Let $f: \mathbb{Z}_p^d\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_p^{d'}$ be a map of $p$-adic manifolds with $d, d'\geq 0$. For any $k\geq 1$, there is an induced map
\begin{equation*}
f^*: C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p^{d'}, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle\rightarrow C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p^d, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle\;,
\end{equation*}
of $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$-algebras. Moreover, the association $f\mapsto f^*$ is compatible with composition and commutes with the evaluation map $\mathrm{ev}$ from \cref{lem:man-eval}.
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
As $f$ is given by $d'$ locally analytic functions $\mathbb{Z}_p^d\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}_p$, we may reduce to the case $d'=1$ by the universal property of the tensor product. As in the previous proof, the map $f: \mathbb{Z}_p^d\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}_p$ can then be written as
\begin{equation*}
f(x_1, \dots, x_d)=\sum_{\underline{n}} a_{\underline{n}}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}
\end{equation*}
with $a_{\underline{n}}\in\mathbb{Z}_p$ such that $v_p(a_{\underline{n}})$ grows faster than $\varepsilon |\underline{n}|$ for some $\varepsilon>0$. By a similar density argument as in the proof of \cref{lem:man-eval}, our task is to show that, given any $\sum_m b_m\binom{y}{m}\in C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$, the expression
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:man-endoscomp}
\sum_m b_m\binom{\sum_{\underline{n}} a_{\underline{n}} \binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}}{m}
\end{equation}
makes sense in the ring $C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p^d, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$. To this end, we may assume that $\pi^{-\varepsilon m}b_m\rightarrow 0$ in the $\pi$-adic topology after possibly lowering $\varepsilon$; furthermore, as in the proof of \cref{lem:man-eval}, we may then increase $k$ to assume that $\varepsilon k\geq \tfrac{1}{p-1}$.

Now first note that
\begin{equation*}
\sum_m b_m\binom{\sum_{\underline{n}} a_{\underline{n}} \binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}}{m}=\sum_m b_m\sum_{\sum_{\underline{n}} m_{\underline{n}}=m} \prod_{\underline{n}} \binom{a_{\underline{n}}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}}{m_{\underline{n}}}
\end{equation*}
by double counting. Writing $a_{\underline{n}}=p^{e_{\underline{n}}} a'_{\underline{n}}$ with $a'_{\underline{n}}\in\mathbb{Z}_p^\times$, the proof of \cref{lem:app-binompseries} shows that
\begin{equation*}
\binom{a_{\underline{n}}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}}{m_{\underline{n}}}=\sum_j \lambda_{\underline{n}, m_{\underline{n}}, j}\binom{a_{\underline{n}}'\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}}{j}
\end{equation*}
for integers $\lambda_{\underline{n}, m_{\underline{n}}, j}$ satisfying
\begin{equation*}
\frac{1}{k}v_p(\lambda_{\underline{n}, m_{\underline{n}}, j})+\varepsilon m_{\underline{n}}\geq \frac{e_{\underline{n}} j}{k}\;.
\end{equation*}
As the $\pi$-adic valuation of $b_m$ grows faster than $\varepsilon m$ and $e_{\underline{n}}$ grows faster than $\varepsilon |\underline{n}|$, we conclude that we may rewrite (\ref{eq:man-endoscomp}) as
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{\substack{\underline{j}=(j_{\underline{n}})_{\underline{n}} \\ \text{almost all $j_{\underline{n}}=0$}}} c_{\underline{j}}\prod_{\underline{n}} \binom{a_{\underline{n}}'\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}}{j_{\underline{n}}}
\end{equation*}
with elements $c_{\underline{j}}\in \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$ whose $\pi$-adic valuation grows faster than $\varepsilon\sum_{\underline{n}} j_{\underline{n}} |\underline{n}|/k$.

To move on, we observe that $\prod_{\underline{n}}\binom{a_{\underline{n}}'\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}}{j_{\underline{n}}}$ is a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-valued polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ in $d$ variables and hence can be written as
\begin{equation*}
\prod_{\underline{n}}\binom{a_{\underline{n}}'\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}}{j_{\underline{n}}}=\sum_{|\underline{i}|\leq \sum_{\underline{n}} j_{\underline{n}}|\underline{n}|} \mu_{\underline{i}}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{i}}
\end{equation*}
for some $\mu_{\underline{i}}\in\mathbb{Z}_p$ by \cref{rem:app-intbasiszpmult}. Using this, we conclude that (\ref{eq:man-endoscomp}) can be written as
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{\underline{i}} c'_{\underline{i}}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{i}}
\end{equation*}
for elements $c'_{\underline{i}}\in\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$ whose $\pi$-adic valuation grows faster than $\varepsilon |\underline{i}|/k$ and this now yields the claim using the description of $C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p^d, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$ from \cref{lem:man-zpdla}.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lem-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:man-descent}
The analytic stack $\operatorname{AnSpec} C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$ is equipped with a canonical descent datum along the cover
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\rightarrow \mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}
\end{equation*}
from \cref{cor:norms-pres}.
<!-- end lem-8 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
We first show descent to $\mathcal{N}$, for which we have to give a canonical isomorphism
\begin{equation*}
C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!), \pi\mapsto \pi} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}\cong C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!), \pi\mapsto \pi T} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}\;,
\end{equation*}
which after unravelling definitions comes down to showing that
\begin{equation*}
\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\varepsilon>0} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\left\langle\pi^{\varepsilon} T^{\pm 1}, \pi^{\varepsilon n}\binom{x}{n}: n\geq 0\right\rangle\cong \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\varepsilon>0} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\left\langle\pi^{\varepsilon} T^{\pm 1}, (\pi T)^{\varepsilon n}\binom{x}{n}: n\geq 0\right\rangle\;.
\end{equation*}
To establish this, we will show that the filtered systems on both sides are cofinal. Namely, given
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{m, n} a_{mn} T^m\binom{x}{n}\in \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\left\langle\pi^{\varepsilon} T^{\pm 1}, \pi^{\varepsilon n}\binom{x}{n}: n\geq 0\right\rangle\;,
\end{equation*}
we have $v_\pi(a_{mn})-\varepsilon(|m|+n)\rightarrow\infty$ as $|m|+n\rightarrow\infty$ and may assume $\varepsilon<1$ without loss of generality. Then $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon/2$ satisfies 
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
v_\pi(a_{mn})-\varepsilon'(|m-\lfloor n\varepsilon\rfloor|+n)&\geq v_\pi(a_{mn})-\varepsilon'(|m|+\lfloor n\varepsilon\rfloor +n) \\
&\geq v_\pi(a_{mn})-\varepsilon(|m|/2+(\varepsilon+1)n/2) \\
&\geq v_\pi(a_{mn})-\varepsilon(|m|+n)\rightarrow\infty
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
and hence
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{m, n} a_{mn} T^m\binom{x}{n}=\sum_{m, n} a_{mn} T^{m-\lfloor n\varepsilon\rfloor} T^{\lfloor n\varepsilon\rfloor}\binom{x}{n}\in \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\left\langle\pi^{\varepsilon} T^{\pm 1}, (\pi T)^{\varepsilon n}\binom{x}{n}: n\geq 0\right\rangle\;,
\end{equation*}
as desired. The argument for the other direction is similar. Finally, for the further descent along $\mathcal{N}\rightarrow\mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, note that the action of $\lambda\in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ on
\begin{equation*}
C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\varepsilon>0} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\left\langle\pi^{\varepsilon n} \binom{x}{n}: n\geq 0\right\rangle
\end{equation*}
replaces $\varepsilon$ by $\lambda\varepsilon$, but this does not change the colimit.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:man-lafunctor}
The association $\mathbb{Z}_p^d\mapsto (\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la})^d$ extends to a functor
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\{\text{paracompact $p$-adic manifolds}\}&\rightarrow\{\text{analytic stacks over $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$}\} \\
M&\mapsto M^\mathrm{la}\;.
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Given a paracompact $p$-adic manifold $M$, we can write it as a disjoint union of open balls by \cite[Prop.\ 8.7]{Schneider} using the fact that any open subset of $\mathbb{Q}_p^d$ is a disjoint union of open balls $M=\bigsqcup_{i\in I} B_i$. Noting that $B_i\cong \mathbb{Z}_p^{d_i}$ for each $i\in I$ and some $d_i\geq 0$, we set
\begin{equation*}
M^\mathrm{la}\coloneqq \bigsqcup_{i\in I} \,(\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la})^{d_i}\;.
\end{equation*}
If we can show that this association is well-defined, i.e.\ independent of the chosen cover, then \cref{prop:man-endos} guarantees that it is functorial. 

For well-definedness, we take two covers of $M$ by open balls and can then produce a common refinement which is a cover by disjoint open balls as well. Then we are reduced to proving the following statement: Assume that
\begin{equation*}
\bigsqcup_{i\in I} \,\mathbb{Z}_p^d\xrightarrow{\cong} \mathbb{Z}_p^d
\end{equation*}
is a cover of $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$ by disjoint open balls. Then the induced map
\begin{equation*}
\bigsqcup_{i\in I} \,(\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la}\xrightarrow{\cong} (\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la}
\end{equation*}
is an isomorphism. By compactness we know that $I$ is finite and then we may reduce to the case where all balls have the same radius. From here, we may inductively reduce to the case of the cover
\begin{equation*}
\bigsqcup_{a\in [p]^d} (a+p\mathbb{Z}_p^d)\xrightarrow{\cong} \mathbb{Z}_p^d\;,
\end{equation*}
where $[p]=\{0, 1, \dots, p-1\}$. As disjoint unions commute with base change, we may furthermore reduce to the case $d=1$. Then we have to prove that
\begin{equation*}
\bigsqcup_{a\in [p]} (a+p\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}
\end{equation*}
is an isomorphism.

To check this, we may pull back to the cover $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_k \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$ of $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$. Then we have to show that the map
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:man-decomp}
\begin{split}
C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))&\rightarrow \prod_{a\in [p]} C^\mathrm{la}(a+p\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)) \\
\binom{x}{n}&\mapsto \left(\binom{a+px}{n}\right)_{a\in [p]}
\end{split}
\end{equation}
is an isomorphism after base changing to $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$ for any $k\geq 1$. It suffices to give an inverse and we claim that this is provided by summing the maps
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:man-decompinverse}
\begin{split}
C^\mathrm{la}(a+p\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))&\rightarrow C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle \\
\binom{x}{n}&\mapsto \sum_m\left(\sum_{a+p\ell\leq m} (-1)^{m-a-p\ell}\binom{m}{a+p\ell}\binom{\ell}{n}\right)\binom{x}{m}
\end{split}
\end{equation}
for $a\in [p]$, where we note that the right-hand side is the Mahler expansion of the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-valued function on $\mathbb{Z}_p$ given by $\binom{(x-a)/p}{n}$ if $x\in a+p\mathbb{Z}_p$ and zero otherwise. We point out that we do \emph{not} need to show that this map is multiplicative: Once we know that it is inverse to (\ref{eq:man-decomp}), this will follow from the fact that (\ref{eq:man-decomp}) is a ring map.

We first claim that (\ref{eq:man-decompinverse}) induces a well-defined $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)$-linear map, for which we have to check that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:man-decompinverseconverges}
\sum_n c_n\sum_m\left(\sum_{a+p\ell\leq m} (-1)^{m-a-p\ell}\binom{m}{a+p\ell}\binom{\ell}{n}\right)\binom{x}{m}
\end{equation}
makes sense in $C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$ whenever the $\pi$-adic valuations of $c_n\in\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)$ grow faster than $\varepsilon n$ for some $\varepsilon>0$; without loss of generality, we may assume that $\varepsilon<1/k$. In other words, we have to show that the $\pi$-adic valuation of
\begin{equation*}
\sum_n c_n\sum_{a+p\ell\leq m} (-1)^{m-a-p\ell}\binom{m}{a+p\ell}\binom{\ell}{n}
\end{equation*}
grows at least linearly in $m$. Denoting the inner sum by $b_{mn}$, we notice that $b_{mn}=0$ for $n>(m-a)/p$ and hence the above simplifies to
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{n\leq (m-a)/p} c_n b_{mn}\;.
\end{equation*}

We now estimate the $\pi$-adic valuation of each summand individually. By assumption, we have $v_\pi(c_n)\geq \varepsilon n-C$ for some constant $C\gg 0$. Moreover, by \cref{lem:app-valuationmahlercoeffs}, we have 
\begin{equation*}
v_p(b_{mn})\geq \frac{m-pn}{p-1}-1\;.
\end{equation*}
Since we have base changed to $\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$, we may replace factors $p^k$ by $\pi$ up to a powerbounded element and thus we conclude from the above that
\begin{equation*}
v_\pi(b_{mn})\geq \frac{m-pn}{k(p-1)}-1\;.
\end{equation*}
Overall, this implies
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
v_\pi(c_nb_{mn})&\geq \varepsilon n+\frac{m-pn}{k(p-1)}-C-1=\frac{m}{k(p-1)}+n\left(\varepsilon-\frac{p}{k(p-1)}\right)-C-1 \\
&\geq \frac{m}{k(p-1)}+\frac{m-a}{p}\left(\varepsilon-\frac{p}{k(p-1)}\right)-C-1\geq \frac{m\varepsilon}{p}-C'
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
for some $C'\gg 0$, where the first estimate in the second line uses that $\varepsilon<1/k<p/(k(p-1))$ and $n\leq (m-a)/p$ by assumption. This yields the claimed linear growth of the $\pi$-adic valuation of $\sum_n c_nb_{mn}$ in $m$ and thus the expression (\ref{eq:man-decompinverseconverges}) makes sense in $C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle$, as desired.

It remains to show that the maps (\ref{eq:man-decomp}) and (\ref{eq:man-decompinverse}) are pairwise inverse. As both the source and target are $\pi$-adically separated, it suffices to check this on a dense subset and thus linearity reduces us to checking the identities
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{m\geq 0}\left(\sum_{a\in [p]} \sum_{a+p\ell\leq m} (-1)^{m-a-p\ell}\binom{m}{a+p\ell}\binom{a+p\ell}{n}\right)\binom{x}{m}=\binom{x}{n}
\end{equation*}
for $n\geq 0$ and
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{m\geq 0}\left(\sum_{a+p\ell\leq m} (-1)^{m-a-p\ell}\binom{m}{a+p\ell}\binom{\ell}{n}\right)\binom{a+px}{m}=\binom{x}{n}
\end{equation*}
for $a\in [p]$ and $n\geq 0$ in the ring of formal power series over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For the first identity, we see that the inner double sum on the left-hand side collapses to
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{\ell\leq m} (-1)^{m-\ell}\binom{m}{\ell}\binom{\ell}{n}\;,
\end{equation*}
which is the $m$-th Mahler coefficient of the function $\binom{x}{n}$ on $\mathbb{Z}_p$ and this yields the claim. The second identity is proved similarly: The inner sum is the $m$-th Mahler coefficient of the function on $\mathbb{Z}_p$ given by $\binom{(y-a)/p}{n}$ if $y\in a+p\mathbb{Z}_p$ and zero otherwise and evaluating this for $y=a+px$ yields $\binom{x}{n}$, as desired.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- ex-1: body_md -->
For $M=\mathbb{Q}_p$, we have
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{Q}_p^\mathrm{la}\cong \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_n\,(p^{-n}\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}\;.
\end{equation*}
Indeed, following the proof above, we have
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{Q}_p^\mathrm{la}\cong \bigsqcup_{a\in \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p} (a+\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}\cong \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_n \bigsqcup_{a\in p^{-n}\mathbb{Z}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p} (a+\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}\cong \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_n \,(p^{-n}\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}\;.\qedhere
\end{equation*}
<!-- end ex-1 -->
<!-- ex-2: body_md -->
Assume that $M=G$ is a $p$-adic Lie group. Then the paracompactness is automatic and, by \cite[Thm.\ 8.32]{ProPGroups}, there is an open subgroup $G_0\subseteq G$ such that $G_0\cong \mathbb{Z}_p^d$ as $p$-adic manifolds. This yields
\begin{equation*}
G^\mathrm{la}\cong \bigsqcup_{g\in G/G_0} (gG_0)^\mathrm{la}\;. \qedhere
\end{equation*}
<!-- end ex-2 -->
<!-- lem-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:man-transverseintersect}
Let $M$ be a $p$-adic manifold and assume that $M', M''\subseteq M$ are submanifolds such that the inclusion maps are transverse. If $x\in M'\cap M''$ is any point in the intersection of the two submanifolds, then there is an open neighbourhood $x\in U\subseteq M$ with coordinates $x_1, \dots, x_d$ such that 
\begin{equation*}
M'\cap U=V(x_1, \dots, x_r)\subseteq U\;, \hspace{0.5cm} M''\cap U=V(x_{r+1}, \dots, x_{r+s})\subseteq U
\end{equation*}
for some $r, s\geq 0$ with $r+s\leq d$. In particular, the intersection $M'\cap M''$ is a $p$-adic manifold.
<!-- end lem-9 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
By definition, there is some neighbourhood $x\in U\subseteq M$ with coordinates $x_1, \dots, x_d$ and $\mathbb{Q}_p$-valued analytic functions $f_1, \dots, f_r$ whose derivatives $\mathrm{d}_xf_1, \dots, \mathrm{d}_xf_r$ at $x$ are linearly independent in $(T_xM)^\vee$ such that $M'\cap U$ is cut out by $f_1=\dots=f_r=0$; similarly, we find functions $f_{r+1}, \dots, f_{r+s}$ with linearly independent derivatives at $x$ such that $M''\cap U$ is the common vanishing locus of $f_{r+1}, \dots, f_{r+s}$. Now note that $\mathrm{d}_xf_1, \dots, \mathrm{d}_x f_r$ form a basis of the conormal space $N_x(M'/M)^\vee=\operatorname{Ker}((T_xM)^\vee\rightarrow (T_xM')^\vee)$ and, similarly, $\mathrm{d}_xf_{r+1}, \dots, \mathrm{d}_xf_{r+s}$ form a basis of $N_x(M''/M)^\vee$. As $T_xM'+T_xM''=T_xM$ by assumption, the conormal spaces $N_x(M'/M)^\vee$ and $N_x(M''/M)^\vee$ intersect trivially, hence $\mathrm{d}_xf_1, \dots, \mathrm{d}_xf_{r+s}$ are jointly linearly independent. 

In particular, we have $r+s\leq d$ and, using the derivatives of the coordinate functions $x_i$, we can extend $\mathrm{d}_xf_1, \dots, \mathrm{d}_xf_{r+s}$ to a basis $\mathrm{d}_xf_1, \dots, \mathrm{d}_xf_{r+s}, \mathrm{d}_xg_{r+s+1}, \dots, \mathrm{d}_xg_d$ of $T_xM$. By the inverse function theorem in the form from \cite[Prop.\ 9.3]{Schneider}, the functions $f_1, \dots, f_{r+s}, g_{r+s+1}, \dots, g_d$ then induce an isomorphism from $U$ onto a small open subset of $\mathbb{Q}_p^d$ after possibly shrinking $U$. In these new coordinates $x_1', \dots, x_d'$, we will then have $M'\cap U=V(x_1', \dots, x_r')$ and $M''\cap U=V(x_{r+1}', \dots, x_{r+s}')$ by construction, as desired. For the second part, we just note that $M'\cap M''\cap U=V(x_1, \dots, x_{r+s})$ is a $p$-adic manifold. This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:man-transverse}
Let $M_1\rightarrow M\leftarrow M_2$ be transverse maps of paracompact $p$-adic manifolds. Then the fibre product $M_1\times_M M_2$ has the structure of a $p$-adic manifold and the diagram
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
(M_1\times_M M_2)^\mathrm{la}\ar[r]\ar[d] & M_2^\mathrm{la}\ar[d] \\
M_1^\mathrm{la}\ar[r] & M^\mathrm{la}
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
of analytic stacks over $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is cartesian. In other words, the functor $(-)^\mathrm{la}$ commutes with transverse fibre products.
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Let $f_1: M_1\rightarrow M$ and $f_2: M_2\rightarrow M$ be the given maps. Then first note that $M_1\times_M M_2$ identifies with the intersection of the two submanifolds
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
M_1\times M_2&\hookrightarrow M_1\times M_2\times M\;, \hspace{0.3cm} (x, y)\mapsto (x, y, f_1(x)) \\
M_1\times M_2&\hookrightarrow M_1\times M_2\times M\;, \hspace{0.3cm} (x, y)\mapsto (x, y, f_2(y))
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
of $M_1\times M_2\times M$. By assumption, these are transverse submanifolds and hence their intersection is a $p$-adic manifold by \cref{lem:man-transverseintersect}. As the fibre product $M_1^\mathrm{la}\times_{M^\mathrm{la}} M_2^\mathrm{la}$ can be described similarly and the functor $M\mapsto M^\mathrm{la}$ commutes with finite products by construction, we may thus reduce to the case where $M_1$ and $M_2$ are submanifolds of $M$. Working locally on $M$, we can furthermore assume that $M\cong \mathbb{Z}_p^d$ and $M_1=V(x_1, \dots, x_r)$ while $M_2=V(x_{r+1}, \dots, x_{r+s})$ by \cref{lem:man-transverseintersect}, where $x_1, \dots, x_d$ are the coordinates on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$. By induction, we can furthermore reduce to the case $r=1$ and compatibility with finite products then furthermore reduces us to $r+s=d$. In this case, we have $M\cong M_1\times M_2$ and then the claim follows from compatibility with finite products, so we are done.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- prop-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:man-transmutation}
Let $X$ be a smooth $\mathbb{Z}_p$-scheme. Then $X(\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}$ is the sheafification of the presheaf over $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ given by
\begin{equation*}
R\mapsto X(\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R))\;,
\end{equation*}
where the mapping space on the right is computed over $\mathbb{Z}_p$. Moreover, the same is true if we replace $\mathbb{Z}_p$ by $\mathbb{Q}_p$ everywhere and additionally assume that $X$ is separated and of finite type.
<!-- end prop-8 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
We only do the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-case, the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-case is analogous; the separatedness and finite type assumptions are only in place to ensure that $X(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ is a paracompact $p$-adic manifold. Clearly, the assignment $X\mapsto X(\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}$ satisfies Zariski descent and we first argue that the same is true for the assignment sending $X$ to the sheafification of $R\mapsto X(\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R))$, which we momentarily call $X(\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la})$. As the latter commutes with fibre products in $X$, we only need to show that $\bigsqcup_i U_i(\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la})\rightarrow X(\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la})$ is surjective for any Zariski cover $X=\bigcup_i U_i$. In fact, we are going to show

\bigskip

\textbf{Claim.} For any map $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R)\rightarrow X$, there is a finite decomposition $R\cong\prod_j R_j$ such that each induced map $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R_j)\rightarrow \operatorname{Spec}\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R)\rightarrow X$ factors through a single $U_i$.

\bigskip

\textit{Proof of the claim.} Pulling back the given open cover of $X$ to an open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R)$, we may assume that $X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R)$ and that the map $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R)\rightarrow X$ is the identity. Then $X$ is affine and we may thus assume that the given open cover is by distinguished opens $D(f_i)$.

By \cref{lem:smoothfp-zpladagger} below, the map $\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{Betti}}$ is surjective with kernel contained in $p\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}$, which is in turn contained in the Jacobson radical of the ring stack $\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}$: Indeed, the inversion map $1+p\mathbb{Z}_p\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_p$ is locally analytic, hence induces a map $1+p\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}$ by \cref{prop:man-endos}. Thus, checking whether an element is a unit in $\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R)$ may be done after mapping to $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{Betti}}(R)$. In other words, it suffices to prove the claim for the ring stack $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{Betti}}$ in place of $\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}$.

Now note that $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{Betti}}(R)\cong \operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0 \operatorname{Spec} R, \mathbb{Z}_p)$ with the ring structure induced by the one on $\mathbb{Z}_p$ and where $S\coloneqq \pi_0\operatorname{Spec} R$ is a profinite set. As the $f_i$ generate the unit ideal and $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is local, the open subsets $\{s\in S: f_i(s)\in \mathbb{Z}_p^\times\}$ cover $S$ and we may choose a refinement $S=\bigsqcup_j S_j$ of this cover by finitely many pairwise disjoint clopen subsets of $S$. As $S=\pi_0 \operatorname{Spec} R$, the idempotents of $R$ corresponding to the $S_j$ induce the desired product decomposition $R=\prod_j R_j$ of $R$. \hfill\qedhere

\bigskip

We conclude that both $X(\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}$ and $X(\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la})$ satisfy Zariski descent in $X$. Thus, working Zariski locally on $X$ now, we may assume that $X$ is standard smooth cut out by the equations $f_1=\dots=f_m=0$ in $\mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{Z}_p}$; in particular, the diagram
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
X\ar[r]\ar[d] & \mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{Z}_p}\ar[d, "{(f_1, \dots, f_m)}"] \\
\{0\}\ar[r] & \mathbb{A}^m_{\mathbb{Z}_p}
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
of derived $\mathbb{Z}_p$-schemes is cartesian. As the claim is clearly true for $X=\mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{Z}_p}$, it suffices to check that the diagram
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
X(\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}\ar[r]\ar[d] & (\mathbb{Z}_p^n)^\mathrm{la}\ar[d, "{(f_1, \dots, f_m)}"] \\
\{0\}\ar[r] & (\mathbb{Z}_p^m)^\mathrm{la}
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
is cartesian as well. However, by construction, the Jacobian matrix of $f_1, \dots, f_m$ has full rank everywhere on $X$, i.e.\ the map $(f_1, \dots, f_m): \mathbb{Z}_p^n\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_p^m$ of $p$-adic manifolds induces a surjection onto the tangent space of $\mathbb{Z}_p^m$ at zero. Thus, the $p$-adic manifold $X(\mathbb{Z}_p)$ is the transverse fibre product of $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$ and $\{0\}$ over $\mathbb{Z}_p^m$, whence the claim follows from \cref{prop:man-transverse}.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- rem-6: body_md -->
In fact, using similar arguments, one can prove that the sheafification is not necessary, i.e.\ the assignment $R\mapsto X(\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}(R))$ is already a sheaf.
<!-- end rem-6 -->
<!-- ex-3: body_md -->
Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a smooth algebraic group over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. Then $\mathbb{G}(\mathbb{Q}_p)^\mathrm{la}$ is the transmutation of $\mathbb{G}$ with respect to the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-algebra stack $\mathbb{Q}_p^\mathrm{la}$ over $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$.
<!-- end ex-3 -->
<!-- defi-3: body_md -->
For $h\in\mathbb{R}$,\footnote{In \cite{Porat2}, it is always assumed that $h\geq 0$, but in fact everything works for general $h\in\mathbb{R}$.} we define
\begin{equation*}
C^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B^+)\coloneqq B^+\left\langle\pi^{v^h(\underline{n})}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}: \underline{n}\geq 0\right\rangle\;,
\end{equation*}
where we recall that $\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}\coloneqq \prod_{i=1}^d \binom{x_i}{n_i}$ and $v^h(\underline{n})\coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^d v_p(\lfloor n_i/p^h\rfloor!)$. Similarly, we set
\begin{equation*}
C_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B^+)\coloneqq B^+\left\langle\pi^{v_h(\underline{n})}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}: \underline{n}\geq 0\right\rangle
\end{equation*}
for $v_h(\underline{n})\coloneqq \lfloor |\underline{n}|/p^h(p-1)\rfloor$, where $|\underline{n}|\coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^d n_i$. We let $C^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ and $C_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ denote the base changes of these $B^+$-modules to $B$ and call
\begin{equation*}
C^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)\coloneqq \prod_{g\in G/G_0} C^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(gG_0, B)\;, \hspace{0.3cm} C_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)\coloneqq \prod_{g\in G/G_0} C_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(gG_0, B)
\end{equation*}
the \emph{upper $h$-analytic} and \emph{lower $h$-analytic functions} on $G$, respectively. Finally, the \emph{locally analytic functions} on $G$ are defined by
\begin{equation*}
C^\mathrm{la}(G, B)\coloneqq \prod_{g\in G/G_0} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_h C^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(gG_0, B)=\prod_{g\in G/G_0} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_h C_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(gG_0, B)\;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end defi-3 -->
<!-- rem-7: body_md -->
Note that $C^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$ and $C_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$ depend on the choice of $G_0$ even though this is not apparent from the notation. In contrast, by \cite[Cor.\ 4.31]{Porat2}, the algebra $C^\mathrm{la}(G, B)$ of locally analytic functions on $G$ is independent of the choice of $G_0$.
<!-- end rem-7 -->
<!-- defi-4: body_md -->
For any $h\in\mathbb{R}$, the \emph{$h\dagger$-analytic functions} on $G$ are defined by
\begin{equation*}
C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)\coloneqq \prod_{g\in G/G_0} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h} C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(gG_0, B)=\prod_{g\in G/G_0} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h} C_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(gG_0, B)\;,
\end{equation*}
where the equality is due to \cite[Lem.\ 4.4.2]{Porat2}.
<!-- end defi-4 -->
<!-- rem-8: body_md -->
Note that formally setting $h=\infty$ recovers the definition of locally analytic functions.
<!-- end rem-8 -->
<!-- defi-5: body_md -->
For any $h\in\mathbb{R}$, we define
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
D^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)&\coloneqq \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}}(C^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B), B)\;, \\
D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)&\coloneqq \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}}(C_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B), B)\;.
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
The spaces of \emph{upper $h$-analytic} and \emph{lower $h$-analytic distributions} on $G$ are defined by
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
D^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)&\coloneqq (B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]} D^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B) \\
D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)&\coloneqq (B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]} D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\;,
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
respectively.
<!-- end defi-5 -->
<!-- defi-6: body_md -->
\label{defi:porat-lagcompact}
Assume that $G$ is compact and fix $h\in\mathbb{R}$. For any $V\in\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$, its (derived) \emph{upper $h$-analytic} and (derived) \emph{lower $h$-analytic vectors} are defined by
\begin{equation*}
V^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\coloneqq \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(D^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B), V)\;, \hspace{0.3cm} V_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\coloneqq \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B), V)\;,
\end{equation*}
respectively. We define the (derived) \emph{locally analytic vectors} of $V$ as
\begin{equation*}
V^\mathrm{la}\coloneqq \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_h V^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_h V_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}
\end{equation*}
and call $V$ itself \emph{locally analytic} if the natural map $V^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow V$ is an isomorphism. Finally, we let 
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)\subseteq \mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])
\end{equation*}
denote the full subcategory spanned by locally analytic representations.
<!-- end defi-6 -->
<!-- rem-9: body_md -->
It follows from \cite[Prop.\ 4.29]{Porat2} that the locally analytic vectors do not depend on the choice of $G_0$. One can also deduce this from the description of $V^\mathrm{la}$ from \cref{lem:porat-removenuclear} below.
<!-- end rem-9 -->
<!-- defi-7: body_md -->
\label{defi:porat-hdaggergcompact}
Assume that $G$ is compact and fix $h\in\mathbb{R}$. For any $V\in\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$, its (derived) \emph{$h\dagger$-analytic vectors} are defined by
\begin{equation*}
V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\coloneqq \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h} V^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h} V_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\;.
\end{equation*}
