We call $V$ itself \emph{$h\dagger$-analytic} if the natural map $V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow V$ is an isomorphism and let $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)\subseteq \mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ denote the full subcategory spanned by $h\dagger$-analytic representations.
<!-- end defi-7 -->
<!-- rem-10: body_md -->
Again, we point out that formally setting $h=\infty$ recovers the definition of locally analytic vectors.
<!-- end rem-10 -->
<!-- defi-8: body_md -->
For any $V\in\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square})$, the \emph{locally analytic functions} on $G$ with values in $V$ are defined by
\begin{equation*}
C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)\coloneqq \prod_{g\in G/G_0} C^\mathrm{la}(gG_0, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} V\;.
\end{equation*}
Similarly, we define the \emph{$h\dagger$-analytic functions} on $G$ with values in $V$ as
\begin{equation*}
C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, V)\coloneqq \prod_{g\in G/G_0} C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(gG_0, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} V
\end{equation*}
for any $h\in\mathbb{R}$.
<!-- end defi-8 -->
<!-- rem-11: body_md -->
If $G$ is compact, we have $C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)\cong C^\mathrm{la}(G, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} V$ and similarly $C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, V)\cong C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} V$ for any $h\in\mathbb{R}$.
<!-- end rem-11 -->
<!-- lem-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:porat-removenuclear}
Let $G$ be a compact Lie group and $V\in\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item There is an isomorphism
\begin{equation*}
V^\mathrm{la}\cong\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(B, C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)_{\star_{1, 3}})\;,
\end{equation*}
where the subscript $(-)_{\star_{1, 3}}$ indicates that $G$ acts on $C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)$ according to $g.(f\otimes v)=f(g^{-1}(-))\otimes gv$.
\item For any $h\in\mathbb{R}$, there is an isomorphism 
\begin{equation*}
V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\cong\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(B, C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, V)_{\star_{1, 3}})\;.
\end{equation*}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-10 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
We only prove the second part, the first part is proved by formally setting $h=\infty$ in the proof below. Unravelling definitions and using that $B$ is compact as a $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]$-module, which e.g.\ follows from \cite[Thm.\ 6.2]{Porat2}, we have to prove that 
\begin{equation*}
\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h} \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B), V)\cong \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h} \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(B, C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, V)_{\star_{1, 3}})\;.
\end{equation*}
In turn, this would follow from
\begin{equation*}
\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h}  \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_B(D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B), V)\cong \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h} C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} V
\end{equation*}
by applying $\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(B, -)$ and again using that $B$ is a compact $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]$-module.

However, as $D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$ is the $B$-linear dual of $C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$ by definition, there is a natural map 
\begin{equation*}
C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} V\rightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_B(D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B), V)
\end{equation*}
and our task is to show that it becomes an isomorphism after taking colimits over $h'<h$. To this end, as both $D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$ and $C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$ are a finite direct sum of copies of $D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ and $C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$, respectively, we may assume that $G=G_0$. We claim that the desired isomorphism follows once we prove that the transition maps $C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\rightarrow C^{h''\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ for $h'<h''<h$ are trace-class. To see this, we write $C^{h'}\coloneqq C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ and $D^{h'}\coloneqq D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ to ease notation and similarly for $h''$; moreover, we will implicitly take all tensor products over $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}$ in the following. Then the definition of trace-class maps tells us that $C^{h'}\rightarrow C^{h''}$ is induced by a map $\eta: B\rightarrow D^{h'}\otimes C^{h''}$ and hence we obtain a commutative diagram
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
C^{h'}\otimes V\ar[r, "\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta\otimes\operatorname{id}"]\ar[d] & C^{h'}\otimes D^{h'}\otimes C^{h''}\otimes V\ar[r, "\mathrm{ev}\otimes\operatorname{id}\otimes\operatorname{id}"]\ar[d] & C^{h''}\otimes V\ar[d, equals] \\
\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_B(D^{h'}, V)\ar[r, "\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta"] & \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_B(D^{h'}, V)\otimes D^{h'}\otimes C^{h''}\ar[r, "\mathrm{ev}\otimes\operatorname{id}"] & V\otimes C^{h''}\makebox[0pt][l]{\;.}
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
In particular, we see that the map $C^{h'}\otimes V\rightarrow C^{h''}\otimes V$ factors through $\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_B(D^{h'}, V)$ and hence the natural map $C^{h'}\otimes V\rightarrow\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_B(D^{h'}, V)$ indeed induces an isomorphism on colimits over $h'<h$ by cofinality.

It thus remains to show that the maps $C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\rightarrow C^{h''\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ are indeed trace-class. For this, recall that
\begin{equation*}
C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\cong B^+\left\langle \pi^{v^{h'}(\underline{n})}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}: \underline{n}\geq 0\right\rangle\otimes_{B^+} B\;.
\end{equation*}
In particular, we see that
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{\underline{n}} \left(\pi^{v^{h'}(\underline{n})}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}\right)^\vee\in D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\;,
\end{equation*}
where $(-)^\vee$ denotes the dual vector; in other words, the dual vectors of $\pi^{v^{h'}(\underline{n})}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}$ form a nullsequence in $D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$. As the $\pi^{v^{h'}(\underline{n})}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}$ form a nullsequence in $C^{h''\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ for any $h'<h''<h$, we see that 
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{\underline{n}} \left(\pi^{v^{h'}(\underline{n})}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}\right)^\vee\otimes\pi^{v^{h'}(\underline{n})}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}
\end{equation*}
makes sense in $D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} C^{h''\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ as nullsequences are summable in solid abelian groups. As the map $B\rightarrow D^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} C^{h''\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ classifying this sum induces the map $C^{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\rightarrow C^{h''\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$, we are done.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- rem-12: body_md -->
Note that the analogue of \cref{lem:porat-removenuclear} for (both upper and lower) $h$-analytic instead of locally analytic vectors is stated in \cite[Prop.\ 5.4]{Porat2} under the assumption that $V$ is nuclear as a $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}$-module. The key idea above is that one can get rid of the nuclearity assumption by taking the colimit over $h$.
<!-- end rem-12 -->
<!-- defi-9: body_md -->
Let $G$ be an arbitrary $p$-adic Lie group, possibly non-compact, and $V$ a $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]$-module. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The (derived) \emph{locally analytic vectors} $V^\mathrm{la}$ of $V$ are defined as
\begin{equation*}
V^\mathrm{la}\coloneqq\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(B, C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)_{\star_{1, 3}})\;.
\end{equation*}
If the natural map $V^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow V$ is an isomorphism, we call $V$ a \emph{locally analytic} $G$-representation and the corresponding full subcategory of $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ is denoted by $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)$.
\item For any $h\in\mathbb{R}$, the (derived) \emph{$h\dagger$-analytic vectors} $V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ of $V$ are defined as
\begin{equation*}
V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\coloneqq\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(B, C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, V)_{\star_{1, 3}})\;.
\end{equation*}
If the natural map $V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow V$ is an isomorphism, we call $V$ an \emph{$h\dagger$-analytic} $G$-representation and the corresponding full subcategory of $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ is denoted by $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defi-9 -->
<!-- rem-13: body_md -->
By \cref{lem:porat-removenuclear}, we see that the definition above recovers \cref{defi:porat-lagcompact} and \cref{defi:porat-hdaggergcompact}, respectively, in the case where $G$ is compact.
<!-- end rem-13 -->
<!-- lem-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:porat-laopensub}
Let $G'\subseteq G$ be any open subgroup and $V\in\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item We have
\begin{equation*}
V^{G\text{-}\mathrm{la}}\cong V^{G'\text{-}\mathrm{la}}
\end{equation*} 
via the natural map, where $V^{G'\text{-}\mathrm{la}}$ refers to the locally analytic vectors in $V$ as a $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G']$-module.
\item Assume that $G'$ contains $G_0$ as an open subgroup. Then
\begin{equation*}
V^{G\text{-}h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\cong V^{G'\text{-}h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}
\end{equation*}
for any $h\in\mathbb{R}$ via the natural map.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-11 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
We only prove (ii), the proof of (i) is then formally obtained by setting $h=\infty$. By construction, we have
\begin{equation*}
C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, V)=\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G']}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G], C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G', V))\;.
\end{equation*}
Thus, we compute
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
V^{G\text{-}h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}&=\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(B, C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, V)_{\star_{1, 3}}) \\
&\cong \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(B, \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G']}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G], C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G', V))) \\
&\cong \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G']}(B, C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G', V)_{\star_{1, 3}})=V^{G'\text{-}h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
using the tensor-hom adjunction.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:porat-colimsla}
The endofunctors $V\mapsto V^\mathrm{la}$ and $V\mapsto V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ of the category $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ commute with all colimits.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
By \cref{lem:porat-laopensub}, we may assume that $G$ is compact. Then $B$ is compact as a $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]$-module by \cite[Thm.\ 6.2]{Porat2} and this implies the claim as $V\mapsto C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)=C^\mathrm{la}(G, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} V$ and $V\mapsto C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)=C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} V$ commute with colimits in $V$.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lem-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:porat-dlagenerators}
Assume that $G$ is compact. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The category $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}}^\mathrm{la} G)$ is the full subcategory of $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ generated under colimits by objects $V\in\mathcal{D}(D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B))$ for varying $h\in\mathbb{R}$.
\item For any $h\in\mathbb{R}$, the category $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}} G)$ is the full subcategory of $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ generated under colimits by objects $V\in\mathcal{D}(D_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B))$ for varying $h'<h$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-12 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Again, we only prove (ii) as the proof of (i) is then obtained by formally setting $h=\infty$. By \cref{cor:porat-colimsla}, we see that $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}} G)$ is indeed stable under colimits. As the $D_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$ are idempotent, the claim immediately follows from $V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h} V_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ and $V_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}=\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(D_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B), V)$ for any $V\in\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ by definition.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- lem-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:porat-laidempotent}
For all $h\leq h'$, we have 
\begin{equation*}
(V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}})^{h'\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\cong V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\cong (V^{h'\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}})^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}
\end{equation*}
via the natural maps. Similarly, we have 
\begin{equation*}
(V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}})^\mathrm{la}\cong V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\cong (V^\mathrm{la})^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}
\end{equation*}
and $(V^\mathrm{la})^\mathrm{la}\cong V^\mathrm{la}$. In particular, any $h\dagger$-analytic representation is $h'\dagger$-analytic for all $h'\geq h$ and locally analytic.
<!-- end lem-13 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
By \cref{lem:porat-laopensub}, we may assume that $G$ is compact. As $(-)^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ and $(-)^\mathrm{la}$ commute with colimits by \cref{cor:porat-colimsla}, it then suffices to show that 
\begin{equation*}
(V_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}})_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\cong V_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\cong (V_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}})_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}
\end{equation*}
for all $h\leq h'$ via the natural maps. However, by definition, we have
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
(V_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}})_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}&=\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(D_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B), \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B), V)) \\
&\cong \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(D_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]} D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B), V) \\
&\cong \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B), V)=V_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\;,
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
where the first isomorphism in the last row uses that $D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$ is an idempotent $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]$-algebra and $D_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$ is a $D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$-module. One similarly proves that $(V_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}})_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\cong V_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ and this finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:porat-adjunction}
The functors $V\mapsto V^\mathrm{la}$ and $V\mapsto V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ are right-adjoint to the inclusions 
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}}^\mathrm{la} G)\hookrightarrow \mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]) \hspace{0.3cm}\text{and}\hspace{0.3cm} \mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}} G)\hookrightarrow \mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])\;,
\end{equation*}
respectively.
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
We have $V^\mathrm{la}\in \mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}}^\mathrm{la} G)$ and $V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\in \mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}} G)$ by \cref{lem:porat-laidempotent}, so it suffices to give the units and counits of the adjunctions. However, the counits are the natural maps $V^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow V$ and $V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow V$, respectively, and the units come from the fact that these maps are isomorphisms if $V$ is locally analytic or $h\dagger$-analytic, respectively.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lem-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:porat-cohdimla}
The cohomological dimensions of the endofunctors $V\mapsto V^\mathrm{la}$ and $V\mapsto V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ of $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ are bounded by $\dim G$.
<!-- end lem-14 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
By \cref{lem:porat-laopensub}, we may assume that $G=G_0$. Then first observe that the functor $V\mapsto C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)$ has cohomological dimension zero as $C^\mathrm{la}(G, B)$ is flat over $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}$, and similarly for $V\mapsto C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, V)$. Indeed, this is because $C^\mathrm{la}(G, B)=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_h C^{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$ is a colimit of $B$-Banach spaces. Thus, \cref{lem:porat-removenuclear} reduces us to proving that $\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]}(B, -)$ has cohomological dimension bounded by $\dim G$, but this follows from the Lazard--Serre resolution, see \cite[Thm.\ 6.2]{Porat2}.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lem-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:porat-underivedla}
An object $V\in \mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ is locally analytic if and only if $H^i(V)$ is locally analytic for all $i\in\mathbb{Z}$. In particular, the $t$-structure on $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ induces a $t$-structure on $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)$. The same holds for $h\dagger$-analytic representations for any $h\in\mathbb{R}$.
<!-- end lem-15 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
We only prove the second part, the first is proved by formally setting $h=\infty$ in the proof below. By \cref{lem:porat-laopensub}, we may without loss of generality assume that $G$ is compact. If $V$ is $h\dagger$-analytic, then $V=V^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h} V_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ and hence $H^i(V)=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{h'<h} H^i(V_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}})$. As $V_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ and hence $H^i(V_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}})$ is a $D_{h'\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, B)$-module, we conclude that $H^i(V)$ is $h\dagger$-analytic by \cref{lem:porat-dlagenerators}. Conversely, assume that $H^i(V)$ is $h\dagger$-analytic for all $i\in\mathbb{Z}$. By \cref{lem:porat-cohdimla}, we may assume that $V$ is a bounded complex and then induction on the cohomological degree reduces us to the case $V=H^0(V)$ using stability of $h\dagger$-analytic representations under shifts and colimits, in which case the claim is clear.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- defi-10: body_md -->
We let $\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$ and $\operatorname{Rep}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$ denote the hearts of the $t$-structures on $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)$ and $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)$ from \cref{lem:porat-underivedla}, respectively.
<!-- end defi-10 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:porat-heart}
The category $\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$ is a Grothendieck abelian category whose derived category identifies with $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)$. The same is true for $h\dagger$-analytic representations.
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
We only prove the first part, the proof of the second is entirely analogous. To show that $\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$ is a Grothendieck abelian category, it remains to see that it has a small family of generators. However, the category $\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$ is generated by the objects
\begin{equation*}
(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]} D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} (B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[S]
\end{equation*}
for $h\in\mathbb{R}$ and $S$ a light profinite set by \cref{lem:porat-laopensub} and \cref{lem:porat-dlagenerators}.

Now take any $V\in\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$ and an injective resolution $I^\bullet$ of $V$ as a $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]$-module. As the functor $V\mapsto H^0(V^\mathrm{la})$ is right-adjoint to the inclusion $\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G\rightarrow \mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])^\heartsuit$ by \cref{cor:porat-adjunction}, it preserves injective objects and the complex $H^0(I^{\bullet, \mathrm{la}})$ is an injective resolution of $V=H^0(V^\mathrm{la})$ in $\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$. In particular, we conclude that the derived internal $\operatorname{Hom}$ in $\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$ agrees with the one in $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])^\heartsuit$. This yields the claim using the fact that $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)$ is left-complete by \cref{lem:porat-cohdimla}.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lem-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:porat-comodules}
There is an equivalence between $\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$ and the abelian category of comodules over the endofunctor $V\mapsto C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)$ of $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square})^\heartsuit$. Similarly, the category $\operatorname{Rep}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$ is equivalent to the abelian category of comodules over the endofunctor $V\mapsto C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G, V)$ of $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square})^\heartsuit$.
<!-- end lem-16 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
We only prove the first part, the second part is entirely analogous. First assume that $V\in\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square})^\heartsuit$ is a $C^\mathrm{la}(G, -)$-comodule. Then the coaction $V\rightarrow C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)$ yields a natural map $V\rightarrow\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_B(D^\mathrm{la}(G, B), V)$, which corresponds to a map $D^\mathrm{la}(G, B)\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} V\rightarrow V$ by adjunction; here we write $D^\mathrm{la}(G, B)$ for the $B$-linear dual of $C^\mathrm{la}(G, B)$. In particular, precomposing this map with $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]\rightarrow D^\mathrm{la}(G, B)$ endows $V$ with the structure of a $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]$-module. Moreover, one easily sees that the coaction map $V\rightarrow C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)$ then lands in the invariants of the $\star_{1, 3}$-action of $G$ on the target. Thus, we conclude that $V$ is a retract of $V^\mathrm{la}$ and hence itself locally analytic, i.e.\ $V\in\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$. Conversely, given $V\in\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G$, the orbit map $V\rightarrow C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)$ turns $V$ into a $C^\mathrm{la}(G, -)$-comodule and one easily sees that these constructions are mutually inverse, which concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:porat-recogniselocan}
Let $V^+\in \mathcal{D}(B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$ be $\pi$-complete and static and assume that there exists some $m\geq 0$ with
\begin{equation*}
(g-1)^mv\in \pi V^+
\end{equation*}
for all $v\in V^+$ and $g\in G$. Then the representation $V\coloneqq V^+\otimes_{B^+} B$ is locally analytic. The same is true if there is some $m\geq 0$ such that
\begin{equation*}
(g-1)^m v\in p V^+
\end{equation*}
for all $v\in V^+$ and $g\in G$.
<!-- end prop-10 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
First note that the second condition implies the first as $\pi$ divides $p$ in $B^+$ by our standing slope assumption. Without loss of generality, we can assume that $G=G_0$ is uniform. Choosing an isomorphism $G_0\cong \mathbb{Z}_p^d$, we obtain elements $g_1, g_2, \dots, g_d\in G_0$ such that any element $g\in G_0$ is of the form $g=\prod_i g_i^{x_i}$ for some $x_i\in \mathbb{Z}_p$. For any fixed $v\in V^+$, one easily shows by induction that
\begin{equation*}
gv=\sum_{\underline{n}} \binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}(g_1-1)^{n_1}\cdots (g_d-1)^{n_d}v
\end{equation*}
for any $d$-tuple $\underline{x}=(x_1, \dots, x_d)$ of integers and then the formula also holds for $x_i\in\mathbb{Z}_p$ by continuity. By assumption, we know that $(g_1-1)^{n_1}\cdots (g_d-1)^{n_d}v$ is divisible by $\pi$ at least $|\underline{n}|/m$ times and hence the orbit map of $v$ yields an element in $C^\mathrm{la}(G, V)$ by definition. Thus, the assignment $v\mapsto (g\mapsto gv)$ yields a section of the map $V^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow V$ and we conclude that $V$ is a retract of a locally analytic representation, hence itself locally analytic. This finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- ex-4: body_md -->
\label{ex:porat-adjointlocan}
For any uniform $p$-adic Lie group $G_0$ of dimension $d$, there is an associated Lie algebra $\Lambda(G_0)$ defined in \cite[§7.2]{ProPGroups}, whose underlying $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module is free of rank $d$. There is an adjoint action of $G_0$ on $\Lambda(G_0)$ which recovers the usual adjoint action on $\mathfrak{g}_0=\Lambda(G_0)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p} \mathbb{Q}_p$. By \cite[§9, Exc.\ 10]{ProPGroups}, this action satisfies the condition from \cref{prop:porat-recogniselocan} and thus $\Lambda(G_0)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p} B$ is a locally analytic representation of $G_0$.
<!-- end ex-4 -->
<!-- rem-14: body_md -->
Note that $G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ does \emph{not} descend further to $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ as the $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$-action changes the value of $h$.
<!-- end rem-14 -->
<!-- defi-11: body_md -->
Let $(B, B^+)$ be a complete Tate Huber pair for which the canonical map $\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow \mathcal{N}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ from \cref{rem:norms-maptatehuber} factors through $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item A $(B, B^+)$-linear \emph{locally analytic representation} of $G$ is defined to be an object of the category 
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^\mathrm{la})\;,
\end{equation*}
where the quotient is by the trivial action of $G^\mathrm{la}$. 

\item If the map $\operatorname{AnSpec} (B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is in addition equipped with a lift to $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}$, we define a $(B, B^+)$-linear \emph{$h\dagger$-analytic representation} of $G$ to be an object of 
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}})
\end{equation*}
for any $h\in\mathbb{R}$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defi-11 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:locan-compareporat}
Assume that $(B, B^+)$ is a complete Tate Huber pair over $(\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!), \mathbb{Z}[\![\pi]\!])$ of slope $\geq 1$ which is residually of finite type. Then pullback along $\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^\mathrm{la}$ induces an equivalence
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^\mathrm{la})\cong \mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)\;.
\end{equation*}
Similarly, pullback along $\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ induces an equivalence 
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}})\cong \mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)
\end{equation*}
for any $h\in\mathbb{R}$.
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
We prove the first part, the second is entirely analogous. For simplicity, write $*\coloneqq\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}$ and work over this base throughout. Noting that $G^\mathrm{la}/G_0^\mathrm{la}\cong G/G_0$ is the Betti stack of a discrete set and using \cref{lem:porat-laopensub}, we are reduced to the case $G=G_0$ by descent along $*/G_0^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow */G^\mathrm{la}$. In this case, by \cref{prop:porat-heart} and \cref{lem:porat-comodules}, we have to show that
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(*/G_0^\mathrm{la})\cong \mathcal{D}(\operatorname{CoMod}_{C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B)}(\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square})^\heartsuit))\;.
\end{equation*}
For this, note that $C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B)$ is a flat $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}$-module as it is a colimit of $B$-Banach spaces in the sense of \cite[Def.\ 3.12]{Porat2}. Together with the fact that $G_0^\mathrm{la}=\operatorname{AnSpec} C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B)$ is prim as $C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B)$ has the induced analytic ring structure from $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}$, this implies that $\mathcal{D}(*/G_0^\mathrm{la})$ identifies with the derived category of the abelian category of descent data along $*\rightarrow */G_0^\mathrm{la}$ by \cite[Prop.\ A.1.2]{MannThesis}. As the latter is equivalent to the abelian category of $C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B)$-comodules in $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square})^\heartsuit$, we are done.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- cor-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:locan-embedgreps}
Let $\mathcal{O}[G]$ denote the algebra object in $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})$ or $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1})$, respectively, obtained by pulling back $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}[G]$ from $\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$. Then there are fully faithful embeddings
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(*/G^\mathrm{la})\hookrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal{O}[G]}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}))\;, \hspace{0.3cm} \mathcal{D}(*/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal{O}[G]}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}))
\end{equation*}
for all $h\in\mathbb{R}$, where $*=\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ or $*=\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}$, respectively. In particular, the pushforwards along
\begin{equation*}
*/G^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow \mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\hspace{0.5cm}\text{and}\hspace{0.5cm}*/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}
\end{equation*}
compute condensed $G$-cohomology.
<!-- end cor-4 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
In the construction of $G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ above, we have given a family of Banach pairs $(B, B^+)$ over $(\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!), \mathbb{Z}[\![\pi]\!])$ which are residually of finite type and of slope $\geq 1$ together with maps $\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}$ which jointly cover $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}$. Then the claim follows using \cref{thm:locan-compareporat} by descending the fact that $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{la}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)$ and $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)$ are full subcategories of $\mathcal{D}((B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G])$. Finally, the last assertion is deduced by comparing internal $\operatorname{Hom}$ under the fully faithful embeddings above.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lem-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:locan-pushforward}
Assume that $(B, B^+)$ is a complete Tate Huber pair over $(\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!), \mathbb{Z}[\![\pi]\!])$ of slope $\geq 1$ which is residually of finite type. For any $h\in\mathbb{R}$, pushforward along the map
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}
\end{equation*}
identifies with the functor $(-)^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ under the equivalence from \cref{thm:locan-compareporat}. The same is true for pushforward along the map
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^{h'\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}
\end{equation*}
for any $h'\geq h$.
<!-- end lem-17 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
We only prove the second part, the proof of the first part is entirely analogous. For this, note that pullback identifies with the forgetful functor
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)\hookrightarrow \mathcal{D}(\operatorname{Rep}^{h'\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}} G)
\end{equation*}
and hence pushforward identifies with the right-adjoint of this forgetful functor, which is given by $(-)^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ by \cref{cor:porat-adjunction}, as desired.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- ex-5: body_md -->
We give a nontrivial example of an object in the category $\mathcal{D}(*/\mathbb{Z}_p^{\times, \mathrm{la}})$, where $*\coloneqq\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$. For this, first note that there is a universal norm (up to rescaling) 
\begin{equation*}
|\cdot|: \mathbb{P}^1\rightarrow [0, \infty]/\mathbb{R}_{>0}
\end{equation*}
over $*=\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ and we let $\accentset{\circ}{\mathbb{D}}$ be the preimage of $[0, 1)/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ under this map. Letting $T$ denote the coordinate on $\mathbb{P}^1$, we observe that there is an action of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\times, \mathrm{la}}$ on $\accentset{\circ}{\mathbb{D}}$ given by 
\begin{equation*}
x.T\coloneqq (1+T)^x-1=\sum_{n\geq 1} \binom{x}{n}T^n
\end{equation*}
for $x\in\mathbb{Z}_p^\times$; indeed, the right-hand side is a locally analytic function since $T^n$ has exponential decay on $\accentset{\circ}{\mathbb{D}}$ with respect to the norm. Using this action, we obtain a map $f: \accentset{\circ}{\mathbb{D}}/\mathbb{Z}_p^{\times, \mathrm{la}}\rightarrow */\mathbb{Z}_p^{\times, \mathrm{la}}$ and we can consider
\begin{equation*}
f_!\mathcal{O}\in\mathcal{D}(*/\mathbb{Z}_p^{\times, \mathrm{la}})\;.
\end{equation*}
Let us make this representation a little more explicit by pulling back along $\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}(\!(\pi)\!)\rightarrow\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$. Then we have
\begin{equation*}
\accentset{\circ}{\mathbb{D}}_{\mathbb{F}_p(\!(\pi)\!)}=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_k \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{T^k}{\pi}\rangle\;,
\end{equation*}
which is exactly the complement of the closed embedding
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1}\xrightarrow{i} \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T\rangle_{\leq 1}\;.
\end{equation*}
As both source and target of $i$ are weakly cohomologically proper over $\operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}(\!(\pi)\!)$, we can use excision to compute the compactly supported cohomology of $\mathbb{D}_{\mathbb{F}_p(\!(\pi)\!)}$ as
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{fib}(\mathbb{F}_p(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T\rangle_{\leq 1}\rightarrow \mathbb{F}_p(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T^{\pm 1}\rangle_{\leq 1})=T^{-1}\mathbb{F}_p(\!(\pi)\!)\langle T^{-1}\rangle_{\leq 1}[-1]
\end{equation*}
and hence $f_!\mathcal{O}$ is concentrated in degree $1$. Computing the action of $\mathbb{Z}_p^\times$ on the first few powers of $T^{-1}$, we get
\begin{equation*}
x.T^{-1}=x^{-1}T^{-1}\;, \hspace{0.5cm} x.T^{-2}=x^{-2}T^{-2}-(x-1)x^{-2}T^{-1}\;, \hspace{0.5cm} \dots
\end{equation*}
In particular, we see that the action of $\mathbb{Z}_p^\times$ is not smooth.
<!-- end ex-5 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:smoothfp-main}
Let $G$ be a $p$-adic Lie group. For any solid $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra $B$, there is a fully faithful embedding
\begin{equation*}
\widehat{\mathcal{D}}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{sm}_B G)\hookrightarrow \mathcal{D}((\mathcal{N}_B/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G^\mathrm{la})\;,
\end{equation*}
where $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{sm}_B G)$ denotes the left-complete derived category of smooth $G$-representations on solid $B$-modules.
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- defi-12: body_md -->
For any locally profinite group $G$, we let $G^\mathrm{sm}$ denote the analytic stack $G^\mathrm{Betti}$.
<!-- end defi-12 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
For any locally profinite group $G$ and any solid $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra $B$, there is an equivalence of categories
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{AnSpec} B/G^\mathrm{sm})\cong \widehat{\mathcal{D}}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{sm}_B G)\;,
\end{equation*}
where we use the induced analytic ring structure on $B$ from $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$.
<!-- end prop-11 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
By definition, the assignment $X\mapsto \mathcal{D}(X^\mathrm{Betti}\times\operatorname{AnSpec} B)$ for light condensed anima $X$ agrees with the six-functor formalism of $\Lambda$-valued sheaves on light condensed anima from \cite[§3.5]{HeyerMann} for $\Lambda$ being the analytic ring $B$.\footnote{Note that all results and constructions from loc.\ cit.\ also work for $\Lambda$ being an analytic ring.} Then the claim is \cite[Prop.\ 5.1.12]{HeyerMann}.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- prop-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:smoothfp-lazardserre}
Let $G_0$ be a uniform $p$-adic Lie group of dimension $d$. For any solid $\mathbb{Z}_p$-algebra $B^+$, there is a resolution
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=small]
0\ar[r] & B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]^{\binom{d}{d}}\ar[r] & B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]^{\binom{d}{d-1}}\ar[r]& \cdots\ar[r] & B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]^{\binom{d}{0}}\ar[r] & B^+
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
of the trivial representation of $G_0$.
<!-- end prop-12 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
See \cite[Thm.\ 5.7]{SolidLocAnReps1}.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- prop-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:smoothfp-kohlhaase}
Let $G_0$ be a uniform $p$-adic Lie group of dimension $d$ and let $h\geq 0$. For any complete Tate Huber pair $(B, B^+)$ over $(\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!), \mathbb{Z}[\![\pi]\!])$ of slope $\geq 1$ which is residually of finite type, there is a resolution
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=small]
0\ar[r] & D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)^{\binom{d}{d}}\ar[r] & D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)^{\binom{d}{d-1}}\ar[r]& \cdots\ar[r] & D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)^{\binom{d}{0}}\ar[r] & B
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
of the trivial representation of $G_0$ extending the Lazard--Serre resolution.
<!-- end prop-13 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
See \cite[Prop.\ 6.5]{Porat2}.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lem-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:smoothfp-desc}
Let $G_0$ be a uniform $p$-adic Lie group. Then the morphism 
\begin{equation*}
f: \mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\rightarrow (\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G_0^\mathrm{la} 
\end{equation*}
is prim and $f_*\mathcal{O}\in \mathcal{D}((\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G_0^\mathrm{la})$ is descendable.
<!-- end lem-18 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
As primness can be checked locally on the target, it suffices to check that 
\begin{equation*}
G_0^\mathrm{la}\times_{\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}}\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1} 
\end{equation*}
is prim for all $k\geq 1$, which follows from the fact that this is a map between affine analytic stacks with induced analytic ring structure. 

For the second part, observing that $f_*$ satisfies base change by primness of $f$, we prove descendability of $f_*\mathcal{O}$ after pullback along the maps
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B_k, B_k^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow \mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}
\end{equation*} 
from (\ref{eq:locan-bb+}), which jointly cover the target for $k\geq 1$, and note that our argument will descend. In other words, we show that $f_{k*}\mathcal{O}$ is descendable for all $k$, where
\begin{equation*}
f_k: \operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B_k, B_k^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B_k, B_k^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G_0^\mathrm{la}\;.
\end{equation*}
Unraveling definitions, we see that $f_{k*}\mathcal{O}$ identifies with the regular representation $C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B_k)$ under the equivalence from \cref{thm:locan-compareporat}. Taking the dual of the Kohlhaase resolution from \cref{prop:smoothfp-kohlhaase} and then taking the colimit as $h\rightarrow\infty$, we obtain an exact sequence
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=small]
0\ar[r] & B_k\ar[r] & C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B_k)^{\binom{d}{0}}\ar[r] & \cdots\ar[r] & C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B_k)^{\binom{d}{d-1}}\ar[r] & C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B_k)^{\binom{d}{d}}\ar[r] & 0
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
of locally analytic $G_0$-representations, where $d$ denotes the dimension of $G_0$. This shows that the trivial representation $B_k$ can be obtained from $C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B_k)$ by taking finitely many direct sums, fibres and cofibres, hence $C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B_k)$ is descendable, as desired.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lem-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:smoothfp-glagsmprim}
Let $G_0$ be a uniform $p$-adic Lie group. Then the morphism
\begin{equation*}
f: (\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G_0^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow (\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G_0^\mathrm{sm}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}/G_0^\mathrm{sm}
\end{equation*}
is prim.
<!-- end lem-19 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
To check that $(\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G_0^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow (\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G_0^\mathrm{sm}$ is prim, it suffices to check primness of $\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\rightarrow (\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G_0^\mathrm{sm}$ by combining \cref{lem:smoothfp-desc} with \cite[Cor.\ 4.7.5]{HeyerMann}. However, this is a $G_0^\mathrm{sm}$-torsor and $G_0^\mathrm{sm}=\operatorname{AnSpec} C^\mathrm{sm}(G_0, \mathbb{Z})$ is an affine analytic stack equipped with the induced analytic ring structure from $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$, hence prim over $\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$. It thus remains to check that $(\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G_0^\mathrm{sm}\rightarrow\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}/G_0^\mathrm{sm}$ is prim as well, but this follows from \cref{lem:norms-primmodr}.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lem-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:smoothfp-cohzpla}
For any $d\geq 0$, consider the map
\begin{equation*}
g: (\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la}\times_{\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}} \mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}\;.
\end{equation*}
Then we have
\begin{equation*}
g_*\mathcal{O}\cong \mathbb{F}_p\left[\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}: \underline{n}\geq 0\right]\;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lem-20 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Using a similar calculation as in the proofs of \cref{prop:norms-embed} and \cref{prop:norms-embedzp}, we see that $g_*\mathcal{O}$ is given by the degree zero subspace of $C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p^d, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{F}_p$ with respect to the $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$-action (and the higher cohomology groups vanish). However, this is precisely given by the right-hand side of the claimed isomorphism due to \cref{lem:man-zpdla}.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lem-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:smoothfp-zpladagger}
For any $d\geq 0$, the map
\begin{equation*}
(\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow (\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{sm}\times_{\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}} \mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}
\end{equation*}
is surjective with kernel
\begin{equation*}
(0\subseteq (\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la})^\dagger\coloneqq\operatornamewithlimits{lim}_{\underline{x}\mapsto p\underline{x}} (\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la}\;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lem-21 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
The claim immediately reduces to the case $d=1$ by taking products. To prove surjectivity, we can base change along the jointly surjective maps
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{AnSpec}\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}\rightarrow\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}
\end{equation*}
for $k\geq 1$ and then our task is to show that the map
\begin{equation*}
C^\mathrm{sm}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}\rightarrow C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)} \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!)\langle\tfrac{p^k}{\pi}\rangle_{\leq 1}
\end{equation*}
is descendable as all analytic ring structures in sight are induced from $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$. In fact, we claim that already $C^\mathrm{sm}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\rightarrow C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$ is descendable. Indeed, as $C^\mathrm{sm}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_n C^\mathrm{sm}(\mathbb{Z}/p^n, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$, we can use \cite[Prop.\ 2.7.2]{MannThesis} to reduce to showing that the maps $C^\mathrm{sm}(\mathbb{Z}/p^n, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\rightarrow C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$ are descendable of bounded index as $n\geq 1$ varies. However, for each $n$, the map $C^\mathrm{sm}(\mathbb{Z}/p^n, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))\rightarrow C^\mathrm{la}(\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!))$ has a section given by evaluating a locally analytic function on $\mathbb{Z}_p$ on a fixed set of representatives of $\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ in $\mathbb{Z}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_p$ and is thus descendable of index $1$, as desired.

To prove the claim about the kernel, we observe that $*=\operatornamewithlimits{lim}_{x\mapsto px} \mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{sm}=\operatornamewithlimits{lim}_n (p^n\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{sm}$ since the map
\begin{equation*}
\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_n C^\mathrm{sm}(p^n\mathbb{Z}_p, \mathbb{Z})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}_0} \mathbb{Z}
\end{equation*}
is an isomorphism as any locally constant function on $\mathbb{Z}_p$ must become constant on $p^n\mathbb{Z}_p$ for $n\gg 0$. As the kernel of $\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{sm}$ is by definition the pullback of $\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}$ along $*\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{sm}$, the claim follows from $\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{la}\times_{\mathbb{Z}_p^\mathrm{sm}} (p^n\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{sm}\cong (p^n\mathbb{Z}_p)^\mathrm{la}$, which is true by construction.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
As discussed earlier, we will show that pullback along
\begin{equation*}
f: (\mathcal{N}_B/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow (\mathcal{N}_B/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G^\mathrm{sm}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec} B/G^\mathrm{sm}
\end{equation*}
is fully faithful. For this, we may replace $G$ by an open uniform subgroup $G_0\subseteq G$: Indeed, we can describe $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{AnSpec} B/G^\mathrm{sm})$ by descent from $\mathcal{D}(\operatorname{AnSpec} B/G_0^\mathrm{sm})$ and all terms of the resulting \v{C}ech nerve will be finite disjoint unions of copies of $\operatorname{AnSpec} B/G_0^\mathrm{sm}$ since $G/G_0$ is discrete. As the analogous statement also holds for $\mathcal{D}((\mathcal{N}_B/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G^\mathrm{la})$, this establishes the desired reduction.

Replacing $G$ by $G_0$ from now on, we claim that $f$ is prim and has the property that $f_*\mathcal{O}\cong\mathcal{O}$; this will imply the desired full faithfulness by the projection formula. As the claimed property of $f$ is stable under base change, we may reduce to the case $B=\mathbb{F}_p$. Then the primness is the content of \cref{lem:smoothfp-glagsmprim}, so it remains to show that $f_*\mathcal{O}\cong\mathcal{O}$, which we may test after pullback along $\operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}/G_0^\mathrm{sm}$. However, pulling back $f$ along this map yields
\begin{equation*}
f': (\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/(1\subseteq G_0^\mathrm{la})^\dagger\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec} \mathbb{F}_{p, \mathsmaller{\square}}
\end{equation*}
by \cref{lem:smoothfp-zpladagger} and hence our task is to show that
\begin{equation*}
R\Gamma((\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/(1\subseteq G_0^\mathrm{la})^\dagger, \mathcal{O})\cong \mathbb{F}_p\;.
\end{equation*}
Computing the left-hand side via the \v{C}ech nerve of the cover $(\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})\rightarrow (\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/(1\subseteq G_0^\mathrm{la})^\dagger$, it then suffices to prove that
\begin{equation*}
R\Gamma(((1\subseteq G_0^\mathrm{la})^\dagger)^m_{\mathbb{F}_p}, \mathcal{O})\cong \mathbb{F}_p
\end{equation*}
for all $m\geq 0$. As $G_0$ is uniform, we have $((1\subseteq G_0^\mathrm{la})^\dagger)^m\cong (0\subseteq (\mathbb{Z}_p^{mn})^\mathrm{la})^\dagger$ as analytic stacks (but not group stacks!), where $n$ is the dimension of $G_0$, and thus it is furthermore sufficient to show
\begin{equation*}
R\Gamma((0\subseteq (\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la})^\dagger_{\mathbb{F}_p}, \mathcal{O})\cong \mathbb{F}_p
\end{equation*}
for all $d\geq 0$.

To carry out this computation, first recall from \cref{lem:smoothfp-zpladagger} that
\begin{equation*}
(0\subseteq (\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la})^\dagger=\operatornamewithlimits{lim}_{\underline{x}\mapsto p\underline{x}} (\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la}
\end{equation*}
and observe that $(\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la}$ and hence also $(0\subseteq (\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la})^\dagger$ is relatively affine over $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, i.e.\ its pullback to any affine analytic stack over $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is affine. As $\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}/\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is prim over $\mathbb{F}_p$ and hence taking cohomology preserves colimits, we thus see that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
R\Gamma((0\subseteq (\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la})^\dagger_{\mathbb{F}_p}, \mathcal{O})\cong \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\underline{x}\mapsto p\underline{x}} R\Gamma((\mathbb{Z}_p^d)^\mathrm{la}_{\mathbb{F}_p}, \mathcal{O})\cong \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\underline{x}\mapsto p\underline{x}} \mathbb{F}_p\left[\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}: \underline{n}\geq 0\right]
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
by \cref{lem:smoothfp-cohzpla}. Proving that this is isomorphic to $\mathbb{F}_p$ now amounts to showing that, for any nonzero $\underline{n}\geq 0$, there is some $i\gg 0$ with $\binom{p^i\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}=0$, which clearly reduces to the one-variable case $d=1$. 

In this case, our task is to prove that, for any $n>0$, there is some $i$ such that 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:smoothfp-expandpichoosen}
\binom{p^i x}{n}=\sum_{j\leq n} \lambda_j\binom{x}{j}
\end{equation}
with $\lambda_j\in p\mathbb{Z}$ for all $j$. The coefficients $\lambda_j$ in this expansion are uniquely determined integers by \cref{prop:app-intbasis} and the main claim from the proof of \cref{lem:app-binompseries} shows that they satisfy
\begin{equation*}
v_p(\lambda_j)+\frac{n}{p-1}\geq ij\;.
\end{equation*}
Thus, taking $i>n/(p-1)$ ensures $v_p(\lambda_j)\geq 1$ for all $j\geq 1$ and it remains to take care of $\lambda_0$. However, the left-hand side of (\ref{eq:smoothfp-expandpichoosen}) vanishes for $x=0$ while setting $x=0$ on the right-hand side yields $\lambda_0$, so we conclude $\lambda_0=0$.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- rem-15: body_md -->
One easily sees that the argument above works just the same if $B$ is merely a $\mathbb{Z}/p^n$-algebra for some $n\geq 1$, i.e.\ whenever $p^nB=0$ for some $n\geq 1$. In other words, the fully faithful embedding 
\begin{equation*}
\widehat{\mathcal{D}}(\operatorname{Rep}^\mathrm{sm}_B G)\hookrightarrow \mathcal{D}((\mathcal{N}_B/\mathbb{R}_{>0})/G^\mathrm{la})\;,
\end{equation*}
from \cref{thm:smoothfp-main} generalises to all solid $p$-power torsion rings $B$.
<!-- end rem-15 -->
<!-- prop-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:duality-prim}
Assume that $G$ is compact. For any real numbers $h'\geq h$, all morphisms in the diagram
\begin{equation*}
*/G^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow */G^{h'\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow */G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow *
\end{equation*}
are weakly cohomologically proper in the sense of \cite[Def.\ 3.1.19]{dRStack}. In particular, they are prim and there is an identification between lower-$!$ and lower-$*$.
<!-- end prop-14 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
We first show that $f: */G^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow *$ is weakly cohomologically proper. For this, we first observe that pulling back the diagonal $\Delta_f: */G^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow */(G^\mathrm{la}\times G^\mathrm{la})$ of $f$ along $*\rightarrow */(G^\mathrm{la}\times G^\mathrm{la})$ yields the morphism $G^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow *$. As $G^\mathrm{la}$ is an affine analytic stack with induced analytic ring structure from $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$, this shows that $\Delta_f$ is weakly cohomologically proper by \cite[Lem.\ 3.1.21]{dRStack}. Then it remains to show that $f$ is prim. For this, we first observe that $g: */G_0^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow */G^\mathrm{la}$ is prim as it pulls back to $G/G_0\rightarrow *$, which is a finite disjoint union of points, and that $g_*\mathcal{O}$ is descendable in $\mathcal{D}(*/G^\mathrm{la})$. Indeed, after pulling back to $\operatorname{AnSpec} (B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}$ for any Tate Huber pair $(B, B^+)$ over $(\mathbb{Z}(\!(\pi)\!), \mathbb{Z}[\![\pi]\!])$ which has slope $\geq 1$ and is residually of finite type, we can identify $g_*\mathcal{O}$ with the locally analytic representation $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G/G_0]$ of $G$ under the equivalence from \cref{thm:locan-compareporat} and then the map $B\rightarrow (B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G/G_0]$ obtained by adjunction has a $G$-equivariant section given by sending each coset in $G/G_0$ to $1$. Thus, we can reduce to the case $G=G_0$ by \cite[Cor.\ 4.7.5]{HeyerMann}. Here, combining \cref{lem:smoothfp-desc} with another application of \cite[Cor.\ 4.7.5]{HeyerMann} reduces us to showing primness of the identity on the point, which is clear.

An analogous argument as in the previous paragraph also shows weak cohomological properness of $*/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow *$ for any $h\in\mathbb{R}$; indeed, note that also the proof of \cref{lem:smoothfp-desc} readily adapts to the case of $G_0^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ in place of $G_0^\mathrm{la}$. It thus remains to show that the maps $*/G^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow */G^{h'\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ and $*/G^{h'\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow */G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ are weakly cohomologically proper. However, since we already know that both source and target of these maps are weakly cohomologically proper over the point, it suffices to check that the diagonal of $*/G^{h'\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow *$ or $*/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow *$, respectively, is weakly cohomologically proper. As this has already been established in the first paragraph, we are done.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- lem-22: body_md -->
\label{lem:duality-dualisingsheaf}
For any solid $\mathbb{Z}_p$-algebra $B^+$, the $B^+$-linear dual
\begin{equation*}
L\coloneqq \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]}(B^+, B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0])^\vee
\end{equation*}
of the continuous group cohomology of $B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]$ is a free $B^+$-module of rank $1$ concentrated in degree $-d$, where $d$ is the dimension of $G_0$.
<!-- end lem-22 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
By the Lazard--Serre resolution from \cref{prop:smoothfp-lazardserre}, we have
\begin{equation*}
\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]}(B^+, B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0])\cong (B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]^{\binom{d}{0}}\rightarrow B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]^{\binom{d}{1}}\rightarrow\dots\rightarrow B^+_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]^{\binom{d}{d}})\;,
\end{equation*}
where the first term $B_\mathsmaller{\square}^+[G_0]^{\binom{d}{0}}$ sits in degree zero. As the Lazard--Serre resolution is constructed from a Koszul resolution, it is self-dual in the sense that the right-hand side of the above isomorphism is concentrated in degree $d$, where it is given by a free $B^+$-module of rank $1$. This finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- lem-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:duality-dualisingsheaflocan}
The $\mathcal{O}[G_0]$-module $L$ in $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1})$ is locally analytic, i.e.\ it lies in the image of the fully faithful embedding 
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}(*/G_0^\mathrm{la})\hookrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal{O}[G_0]}(\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}))
\end{equation*}
from \cref{cor:locan-embedgreps}. If $G_0$ is abelian, then $L$ is in fact the trivial representation.
<!-- end lem-23 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
We check the claim after pulling back to $\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B_k, B_k^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}$ for all $k\geq 1$. By \cref{lem:duality-dualisingsheaf}, we already know that $L$ is a character of $G_0$ and we claim that it is actually the determinant of the dual of the adjoint representation of $G_0$ from \cref{ex:porat-adjointlocan}. This would imply both claims: The adjoint representation is locally analytic by \cref{ex:porat-adjointlocan} and it is trivial if $G_0$ is abelian. To determine the $G_0$-action on $L$, we may extend scalars along $\mathbb{Z}_p\rightarrow\mathbb{Q}_p$ as $B_k$ is $p$-torsionfree, which then reduces us to showing that
\begin{equation*}
\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(\mathbb{Q}_p, \mathbb{Z}_p)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]}(\mathbb{Q}_p, (\mathbb{Q}_p, \mathbb{Z}_p)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0])^\vee
\end{equation*}
is the determinant of the dual of the adjoint representation of $G_0$. However, this is true by \cite[Eq. (24)]{SolidLocAnReps1}, so we are done.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:duality-main}
The map
\begin{equation*}
*/G^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow *
\end{equation*}
is cohomologically smooth. Moreover, for any $h\in\mathbb{R}$, the map
\begin{equation*}
*/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow *
\end{equation*}
is suave; it is even cohomologically smooth \dots
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \dots if $G$ is abelian or
\item \dots after base change to $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1-\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ and $h$ sufficiently large depending on $\varepsilon$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
First note that we can reduce to the case $G=G_0$ in all cases: Indeed, cohomological smoothness may be checked smooth locally on the source and the map $*/G_0^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow */G^\mathrm{la}$ becomes a finite disjoint union of points after pullback along $*\rightarrow */G^\mathrm{la}$; the same argument works for $*/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$. Moreover, we may also check all assertions after pullback along the charts $\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B_k, B_k^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}\rightarrow \mathcal{N}_{|p|<1}$ from (\ref{eq:locan-bb+}); as $\mathcal{N}_{|p|<1-\varepsilon}$ will eventually lie in the image of a single one of these charts for $k\gg 0$ depending on $\varepsilon$, assertion (ii) then turns into the claim that $\operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B_k, B_k^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}/G^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}\rightarrow \operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B_k, B_k^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}$ will be cohomologically smooth for $h\gg 0$ large enough depending on $k$. Thus, write $*\coloneqq \operatorname{AnSpec}\hspace{1pt}(B_k, B_k^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}$ from now on; for simplicity, we will also abbreviate $(B_k, B_k^+)$ by $(B, B^+)$.

To prove the first assertion, consider the maps $g: */G_0^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow *$ and $f: *\rightarrow */G_0^\mathrm{la}$. Our goal is to apply \cite[Lem.\ 4.2.2.(i)]{dRStack} to prove that $g$ is cohomologically smooth with dualising sheaf $L$. Our task is to produce maps $s: f_!\mathcal{O}\rightarrow L$ and $\eta: g_!L\rightarrow \mathcal{O}$ such that $\eta\circ g_!s$ is the identity. To this end, recall from \cref{prop:duality-prim} that $g_!\cong g_*$ and note that $f$ is weakly cohomologically proper as well by \cite[Lem.\ 3.1.21]{dRStack} as it is a $G_0^\mathrm{la}$-torsor and $G_0^\mathrm{la}$ is affine and equipped with the induced analytic ring structure from $\mathbb{Z}_\mathsmaller{\square}$. Using that $g_*$ computes condensed $G$-cohomology by \cref{cor:locan-embedgreps} and base change for $f_*$, which holds as $f$ is prim, we see that our task unwinds to producing maps
\begin{equation*}
s: C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B)\rightarrow L\;, \hspace{0.5cm} \eta: \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]}(B, L)\rightarrow B
\end{equation*}
with the desired compatibility, where $s$ is supposed to be $G_0$-equivariant.

To produce $s$, we recall that $C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B)=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_h C_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ and hence it suffices to produce compatible maps $C_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\rightarrow L$. As both the source and target are reflexive, it then suffices to produce compatible maps
\begin{equation*}
\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}}(B, (B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0])=L^\vee\rightarrow D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)\;.
\end{equation*}
However, recalling from the proof of \cref{lem:duality-dualisingsheaf} that the left-hand side is given by the complex
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:duality-lvee}
(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]^{\binom{d}{0}}\rightarrow (B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]^{\binom{d}{1}}\rightarrow\dots\rightarrow (B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]^{\binom{d}{d}}\;,
\end{equation}
where the first term sits in degree zero, we see that this admits a canonical map to $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]$ given by projecting onto the degree zero term of the above complex. This yields the desired maps after postcomposing with $(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]\rightarrow D_{h\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)$ and it is clear that this is $G_0$-equivariant.

Now we produce $\eta$. For this, we use the Lazard--Serre resolution from \cref{prop:smoothfp-lazardserre} to write $\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]}(B, L)$ as the complex
\begin{equation*}
L^{\binom{d}{0}}\rightarrow L^{\binom{d}{1}}\rightarrow\dots\rightarrow L^{\binom{d}{d-1}}\rightarrow L^{\binom{d}{d}}\;,
\end{equation*}
where the first term sits in degree zero. However, using the explicit complex computing $L^\vee$ from (\ref{eq:duality-lvee}), we immediately identify the above as $L^\vee\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]} L$ and now the desired map
\begin{equation*}
\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]}(B, L)\cong L^\vee\otimes_{(B, B^+)_\mathsmaller{\square}[G_0]} L\rightarrow B
\end{equation*}
is the adjoint of the identity on $L^\vee$. It is not hard to check that the two maps we have constructed satisfy $\eta\circ g_!s=\operatorname{id}$, as desired.

To prove the second part of the statement, recall from \cref{prop:duality-prim} that $f_h: */G_0^\mathrm{la}\rightarrow */G_0^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ is weakly cohomologically proper and hence $f_{h, !}\cong f_{h, *}$ preserves suave objects by \cite[Lem.\ 4.5.16]{HeyerMann}. As $f_{h, *}$ is given by taking $h\dagger$-analytic vectors by \cref{lem:locan-pushforward} and the trivial representation is $h\dagger$-analytic for all $h\in\mathbb{R}$, we conclude that $f_{h, !}\mathcal{O}\cong \mathcal{O}\in\mathcal{D}(*/G_0^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}})$ and hence $*/G_0^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ is suave. Using \cite[Lem.\ 4.4.9.(ii)]{HeyerMann}, we see that the dualising complex is given by $f_{h, !}L=L^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ and hence we can conclude that $*/G_0^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}$ is cohomologically smooth whenever $L$ is already an $h\dagger$-analytic representation. As $L$ is given by the determinant of the dual of the adjoint representation of $G_0$ by the proof of \cref{lem:duality-dualisingsheaflocan}, it is trivial if $G_0$ is abelian and hence in particular $h\dagger$-analytic for all $h\in\mathbb{R}$; this proves (i). To establish (ii), we note that the character $\chi: G\rightarrow B^\times$ defining the action of $G$ on $L$ is locally analytic since $L$ is and due to 
\begin{equation*}
C^\mathrm{la}(G_0, B)=\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_h C^{h\dagger\text{-}\mathrm{an}}(G_0, B)
\end{equation*}
must in fact be $h\dagger$-analytic for some $h\gg 0$. Consequently, the representation $L$ is $h\dagger$-analytic for some $h\gg 0$, which finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- prop-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-intbasis}
The ring of integer-valued polynomials in one variable has a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis given by the polynomials $\binom{x}{n}$ for $n\geq 0$.
<!-- end prop-15 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
The following proof is taken from \cite[Prop.\ I.1.1]{IntegerPolys}. Clearly, the polynomials $\binom{x}{n}, n\geq 0$ are a $\mathbb{Q}$-basis of $\mathbb{Q}[x]$ and are all integer-valued, so it suffices to show that any integer-valued polynomial $f$ is a $\mathbb{Z}$-linear combination of these. Thus, write
\begin{equation*}
f=\sum_{j=0}^d \lambda_j\binom{x}{j}
\end{equation*}
for uniquely determined $\lambda_j\in\mathbb{Q}$. By induction on $j$, we will prove that, in fact, $\lambda_j\in\mathbb{Z}$. Indeed, we have $\lambda_0=f(0)\in\mathbb{Z}$ and, assuming that $\lambda_j\in\mathbb{Z}$ for $j\leq k<n$, we obtain an integer-valued polynomial
\begin{equation*}
g_k=f-\sum_{j=0}^k \lambda_j\binom{x}{j}=\sum_{j=k+1}^d \lambda_j\binom{x}{j}
\end{equation*}
and it is clear that $\lambda_{k+1}=g(k+1)\in\mathbb{Z}$, which completes the induction step.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- rem-16: body_md -->
\label{rem:app-intbasiszp}
The same proof shows that the polynomials $\binom{x}{n}$ form a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-basis of the ring of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-valued polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ in one variable.
<!-- end rem-16 -->
<!-- prop-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-intbasismult}
The ring of integer-valued polynomials in $d$ variables has a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis given by the polynomials
\begin{equation*}
\binom{x_1}{n_1}\binom{x_2}{n_2}\cdots\binom{x_d}{n_d}
\end{equation*}
for $n_1, \dots, n_d\geq 0$.
<!-- end prop-16 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
See also \cite[Prop.\ XI.1.12]{IntegerPolys}. We use induction on $d$, the base case $d=1$ being the content of \cref{prop:app-intbasis}. Again, the polynomials from the statement are clearly all integer-valued and form a $\mathbb{Q}$-basis of $\mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_d]$, so any integer-valued polynomial $f\in\mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_d]$ may be expressed as
\begin{equation*}
f(x_1, \dots, x_d)=\sum_{\underline{n}} a_{\underline{n}} \binom{x_1}{n_1}\cdots \binom{x_d}{n_d}\;,
\end{equation*}
where $\underline{n}=(n_1, \dots, n_d)$ is a multiindex. Our task is to show that $a_{\underline{n}}\in\mathbb{Z}$.

To prove this, we use induction on the $x_d$-degree of $f$. In the base case, the polynomial $f$ is independent of $x_d$ and hence an integer-valued polynomial in $d-1$ variables, so the claim follows by the induction hypothesis of the ``outer'' induction over $d$. For the induction step, note that
\begin{equation*}
f(x_1, \dots, x_{d-1}, x_d+1)-f(x_1, \dots, x_{d-1}, x_d)=\sum_{\underline{n}: n_d=0} a_{\underline{n}} \binom{x_1}{n_1}\cdots \binom{x_{d-1}}{n_{d-1}}\binom{x_d}{n_d-1}
\end{equation*}
is integer-valued as well and has lower $x_d$-degree than $f$. Thus, we conclude $a_{\underline{n}}\in\mathbb{Z}$ for all $\underline{n}$ by the induction hypothesis and this finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- rem-17: body_md -->
\label{rem:app-intbasiszpmult}
Again, the same proof shows that the polynomials $\binom{x_1}{n_1}\cdots \binom{x_d}{n_d}$ form a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-basis of the ring of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-valued polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ in $d$ variables.
<!-- end rem-17 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:app-mahler}
There is a bijection
\begin{equation*}
\{\text{continuous functions $f: \mathbb{Z}_p\rightarrow\mathbb{Q}_p$}\}\overset{1:1}{\longleftrightarrow}\{\text{nullsequences $(a_n)_n$ in $\mathbb{Q}_p$}\}
\end{equation*}
given by sending a nullsequence $(a_n)_n$ to the function $f: \mathbb{Z}_p\rightarrow\mathbb{Q}_p$ defined by
\begin{equation*}
f(x)\coloneqq \sum_n a_n\binom{x}{n}\;.
\end{equation*}
Conversely, the sequence $(a_n)_n$ can be recovered from $f$ via
\begin{equation*}
a_n=\sum_{\ell\leq n} (-1)^{n-\ell}\binom{n}{\ell}f(\ell)\;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
This is the main result of \cite{Mahler}.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:app-amice}
Let $f: \mathbb{Z}_p\rightarrow\mathbb{Q}_p$ be any continuous function. Then $f$ is analytic on each ball $x+p^h\mathbb{Z}_p$ for $x\in \mathbb{Z}/p^h$ if and only if
\begin{equation*}
v_p(a_n)-v_p(\lfloor n/p^h\rfloor !)\rightarrow \infty
\end{equation*}
as $n\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, $f$ is locally analytic if and only if $v_p(a_n)$ grows at least linearly.
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
The first part is \cite[§10, Cor.\ 2]{Amice}. The second part follows since $v_p(\lfloor n/p^h\rfloor!)\sim \tfrac{n}{p^h(p-1)}$ as $n$ grows, i.e.\
\begin{equation*}
\frac{v_p(\lfloor n/p^h\rfloor!)}{n/p^h(p-1)}\rightarrow 1
\end{equation*}
as $n\rightarrow\infty$.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- rem-18: body_md -->
\label{rem:app-amicemult}
The previous two theorems also have analogues in several variables. In particular, it is also proved in \cite{Amice} that any locally analytic function $f: \mathbb{Z}_p^d\rightarrow\mathbb{Q}_p$ is given by
\begin{equation*}
f(x_1, \dots, x_d)=\sum_{\underline{n}} a_{\underline{n}}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}
\end{equation*}
for $p$-adic integers $a_{\underline{n}}$ whose $p$-adic valuation grows at least linearly in $|\underline{n}|\coloneqq n_1+\dots+n_d$, where $\underline{n}=(n_1, \dots, n_d)$ is a multiindex and we set $\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{n}}\coloneqq \binom{x_1}{n_1}\cdots \binom{x_d}{n_d}$.
<!-- end rem-18 -->
<!-- lem-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-prodbinom}
For all $m, n\geq 0$, we have
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:app-prodbinom}
\binom{x}{m}\binom{x}{n}=\sum_j \binom{x}{j}\binom{j}{m+n-j}\binom{2j-m-n}{j-n}
\end{equation}
as polynomials in $x$, where we use the convention that, for $k, \ell\in\mathbb{Z}$, the binomial coefficient $\binom{k}{\ell}$ is only nonzero if $0\leq \ell\leq k$.
<!-- end lem-24 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Since both sides are polynomials in $x$, it suffices to prove that they agree for all $x\in\mathbb{N}$. In that case, the left-hand side counts the number of pairs $(A, B)$ of subsets of a set $S$ of size $x$ with $|A|=m, |B|=n$. However, we can also count this number in a different way: we first choose the union $A\cup B\subseteq S$, afterwards select the elements of $A\cup B$ that lie in both $A$ and $B$ and finally select those elements of $(A\cup B)\setminus (A\cap B)$ that belong to $A$. If $|A\cup B|=j$, this means that we first select $j$ elements from $S$, for which there are a total of $\binom{x}{j}$ possibilities; then we select the $m+n-j$ elements contained in $A\cap B$ from the $j$ elements of $A\cup B$, for which there are $\binom{j}{m+n-j}$ possibilities; finally we select the remaining $j-n$ elements of $(A\cup B)\setminus (A\cap B)$ which belong to $A$, for which there are $\binom{2j-m-n}{j-n}$ possibilities since $|(A\cup B)\setminus (A\cap B)|=2j-m-n$. Summing over $j=|A\cup B|$, this yields the expression on the right-hand side.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lem-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-binompseries}
For each $n\geq 0$, there is an identity of formal power series of the form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\binom{\sum_{i\geq 0} p^ix_i}{n}=\sum_{|\underline{j}|\leq n} \lambda_{\underline{j}}\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{j}}\;,
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
where each $\lambda_{\underline{j}}$ is an integer, $\underline{j}=(j_0, j_1, \dots)$ is a multiindex with almost all entries zero, for which we set $|\underline{j}|\coloneqq \sum_i j_i$, and we write $\binom{\underline{x}}{\underline{j}}\coloneqq \prod_i \binom{x_i}{j_i}$. Moreover, we have
\begin{equation*}
\frac{1}{k}v_p(\lambda_{\underline{j}})+\varepsilon n\geq \sum_i \frac{i j_i}{k}
\end{equation*}
for any $k\geq 1$ and $\varepsilon>0$ satisfying $\varepsilon k\geq \frac{1}{p-1}$.
<!-- end lem-25 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Notice that, by double counting, we have
\begin{equation*}
\binom{\sum_{i\geq 0} p^ix_i}{n}=\sum_{\substack{(j_i)_i\in\mathbb{N} \\ \sum_i j_i=n}} \prod_{i\geq 0} \binom{p^ix_i}{j_i}
\end{equation*}
and hence, by \cref{prop:app-intbasis}, it suffices to prove the following
\bigskip

\textbf{Claim.} For any $i, j\geq 0$, the binomial coefficient $\binom{p^i x}{n}$ is an integer linear combination of $x, \binom{x}{2}, \dots$ with the property that the coefficient $\lambda_j$ of $\binom{x}{j}$ satisfies 
\begin{equation*}
\frac{1}{k}v_p(\lambda_j)+\varepsilon n\geq \frac{ij}{k}\;.
\end{equation*}

\bigskip

\textit{Proof of the claim.} We first show that, if we expand $\binom{p^i x}{n}$ as a polynomial in $x$ with rational coefficients, then the coefficient $\lambda_j$ in front of $x^j$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:app-padicvalcoeffs}
\frac{1}{k}v_p(\lambda_j)+\varepsilon n\geq \frac{ij}{k}\;.
\end{equation}
To this end, note that expanding the brackets in the expression
\begin{equation*}
\binom{p^ix}{n}=\frac{p^ix(p^ix-1)\cdots (p^ix-(j-1))}{n!}
\end{equation*}
yields
\begin{equation*}
\lambda_j=\pm p^{ij}\sum_{1\leq m_1<m_2<\dots<m_j\leq n-1} \frac{1}{m_1m_2\cdots m_j}
\end{equation*}
and hence, using the given condition on $k$ and $\varepsilon$, our task lies in showing
\begin{equation*}
v_p\left(\sum_{1\leq m_1<\dots<m_j\leq n-1} \frac{1}{m_1\cdots m_j}\right)\geq -\frac{n}{p-1}\;.
\end{equation*}
However, as there are at most $n/p^t$ numbers below $n$ divisible by $p^t$ for each $t\geq 1$, the left-hand side is bounded below by
\begin{equation*}
-\frac{n}{p}-\frac{n}{p^2}-\dots=-\frac{n}{p-1}\;,
\end{equation*}
as desired.

The fact that the polynomial $\binom{p^i x}{n}=\sum_{j\leq n} \lambda_j x^j$ with rational coefficients can be rewritten as an integer linear combination of $x, \binom{x}{2}, \dots$ now follows from \cref{prop:app-intbasis} and we have to check that this rewriting does not disturb the inequality on the $p$-adic valuations of the coefficients that we have established. Going through the proof of loc.\ cit., we see that this rewriting starts by writing
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{j\leq n} \lambda_j x^j=\lambda_n'\binom{x}{n}+\sum_{j<n} \lambda'_j x^j\;.
\end{equation*}
Noting that 
\begin{equation*}
\lambda_n'=n!\cdot\lambda_n\;,
\end{equation*}
we see that $v_p(\lambda_n')\geq v_p(\lambda_n)$ and hence the inequality (\ref{eq:app-padicvalcoeffs}) is still satisfied for $j=n$ and $\lambda_j'$ in place of $\lambda_j$. Moreover, expanding 
\begin{equation*}
\binom{x}{n}=\frac{x(x-1)\cdots(x-(n-1))}{n!}
\end{equation*}
as a rational polynomial in $x$, we see that the $p$-adic valuation of each coefficient is at least as large as the $p$-adic valuation of the leading coefficient. From this, we conclude
\begin{equation*}
v_p(\lambda_j'-\lambda_j)\geq v_p(\lambda_n)
\end{equation*}
for each $j<n$ and hence, using that the $\lambda_j$ satisfy (\ref{eq:app-padicvalcoeffs}), we get
\begin{equation*}
v_p(\lambda_j')\geq \min\{v_p(\lambda_j), v_p(\lambda_n)\}\geq \min\{ij-\varepsilon k n, in-\varepsilon k n\}=ij-\varepsilon k n\;,
\end{equation*}
i.e.\ the inequality (\ref{eq:app-padicvalcoeffs}) is still satisfied for all $j<n$ with $\lambda_j'$ in place of $\lambda_j$. 

Now one repeats the argument iteratively: next, we have to write
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{j<n} \lambda_j'x^j=\lambda_{n-1}''\binom{x}{n-1}+\sum_{j<n-1} \lambda_j''x^j
\end{equation*}
and can use the same argument to show that the $\lambda_j''$ still satisfy (\ref{eq:app-padicvalcoeffs}) etc. This can be done until the whole polynomial is rewritten as a linear combination of $x, \binom{x}{2}, \dots$ and since our initial polynomial in $x$ was integer-valued, this will produce an integer linear combination by \cref{prop:app-intbasis}. As the argument above shows that the coefficients satisfy the desired inequality, we are done.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lem-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-genfunc}
For any $k\geq 0$, there is an identity of formal power series
\begin{equation*}
\frac{1}{(1-T)^{k+1}}=\sum_n \binom{n+k}{k}T^n\;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lem-26 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Using the binomial expansion, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
\frac{1}{(1-T)^{k+1}}=\sum_n \binom{-k-1}{n}(-T)^n=\sum_n \binom{n+k}{n}T^n=\sum_n \binom{n+k}{k}T^n\;,
\end{equation*}
as desired.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lem-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-valuationmahlercoeffs}
Let $a\in \{0, 1, \dots, p-1\}$ and $n\geq 0$. Setting
\begin{equation*}
b_{mn}\coloneqq \sum_{a+p\ell\leq m} (-1)^{m-a-p\ell}\binom{m}{a+p\ell}\binom{\ell}{n}
\end{equation*}
for any $m\geq 0$, we have
\begin{equation*}
v_p(b_{mn})\geq \frac{m-pn}{p-1}-1\;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lem-27 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
We consider the generating function $f_n(T)\coloneqq \sum_m b_{mn}T^m$. By \cref{lem:app-genfunc}, we have
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
f_n(T)&=\sum_m\sum_{a+p\ell\leq m} (-1)^{m-a-p\ell}\binom{m}{a+p\ell}\binom{\ell}{n}T^m=\sum_\ell \binom{\ell}{n}T^{a+p\ell}\sum_{m\geq a+p\ell} \binom{m}{a+p\ell}(-T)^{m-(a+p\ell)} \\
&=\sum_\ell \binom{\ell}{n}T^{a+p\ell}\frac{1}{(1+T)^{a+p\ell+1}}=\frac{T^{a+pn}}{(1+T)^{a+pn+1}}\sum_\ell \binom{\ell}{n}\left(\frac{T}{1+T}\right)^{p(\ell-n)} \\
&=\frac{T^{a+pn}}{(1+T)^{a+pn+1}}\frac{1}{\left(1-\frac{T^p}{(1+T)^p}\right)^{n+1}}=\frac{T^{a+pn}(1+T)^{p-a-1}}{((T+1)^p-T^p)^{n+1}}\;.
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Noting that $(T+1)^p-T^p=1-pT(\,\dots)$, expanding the denominator into a power series then yields
\begin{equation*}
f_n(T)=T^{a+pn}(1+T)^{p-a-1}\sum_\ell \binom{-n-1}{\ell}(pT(\,\dots))^\ell\;.
\end{equation*}
As the $(\,\dots)$ term here is a polynomial in $T$ of degree $p-2$ here, the coefficient in front of the degree $j$ term of the sum must be divisible by $p$ at least $j/(p-1)$ times for every $j\geq 0$. Accounting for the degree $pn+(p-1)$ factor $T^{a+pn}(1+T)^{p-a-1}$ in front, this means that the degree $m$ coefficient of $f_n(T)$ is divisible by $p$ at least
\begin{equation*}
\frac{m-pn-(p-1)}{p-1}=\frac{m-pn}{p-1}-1
\end{equation*}
times, as desired.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
